title: llm
text:
Names for the model list
The Settings page shows a list of models. Each item has a name that people know, such as “Claude Sonnet” or “GPT-5.5”. The model id, such as claude/sonnet, is the value that the settings keep. model_label makes the name from the id. PROVIDERS gives the name of each group in the list, and provider_label reads it. ramabana’s is_local tells if a model runs on this Mac. For Ollama, it looks at the daemon host (the host in config.toml, else $OLLAMA_HOST), and it does not connect to it. Thus a model on an Ollama daemon on another computer has no “a local model” name, and its group is “Ollama on another computer”. Without the models extra, no local model is in the list, so no name says “a local model”.


source

provider_label
def provider_label(
    provider:str, values:tuple=()
)->str:
The name of the provider group in the model list, for the model ids values. An Ollama daemon on another computer is not on this Mac.




source

model_label
def model_label(
    value:str, provider:str='', repo:str=''
)->str:
A name that people know for the model id value; repo is the download of a local model, if known.


Each kind of id gets a plain name. A Claude Code tier gets the word Claude. A local model says so.

test_eq(model_label('claude/sonnet'), 'Claude Sonnet')
test_eq(model_label('claude/claude-opus-5-5'), 'Claude Opus 5.5')
test_eq(model_label('anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'), 'Claude Haiku 4.5')
test_eq(model_label('codex/gpt-6-astra'), 'GPT-6 Astra')
test_eq(model_label('openai/gpt-5.4-mini'), 'GPT-5.4 Mini')
test_eq(model_label('gemini/gemini-3.5-flash'), 'Gemini 3.5 Flash')
test_eq(model_label('qwen-4b', 'mlx', 'mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit'), 'a local model: Qwen 3.5 4B')
test_eq(model_label('gemma-e4b', 'litert', 'litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm'), 'a local model: Gemma 4 E4B')
test_eq(model_label('my-model', 'azure'), 'my-model')

An OpenAI id gets the name that OpenAI uses. A snapshot date such as 2024-07-18 goes, so the name is the same as the name of the model.

test_eq(model_label('openai/gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18'), 'GPT-4o mini')
test_eq(model_label('copilot/gpt-4-o-preview'), 'GPT-4o preview')
test_eq(model_label('openai/gpt-4o'), 'GPT-4o')
test_eq(model_label('openai/gpt-4.1-mini'), 'GPT-4.1 Mini')

The o-series names stay in lower case, with their hyphen:

test_eq(model_label('codex/o4-mini'), 'o4-mini')
test_eq(model_label('openai/o3'), 'o3')

One letter and a number stay together, as the maker writes them:

test_eq(model_label('copilot/kimi-k3'), 'Kimi K3')
test_eq(model_label('openrouter/qwen3-8b'), 'Qwen 3 8B')   # a longer word and a number still get a space

An Ollama model is local only when its daemon is on this Mac. With $OLLAMA_HOST on localhost, the model and its group are on this Mac:

from fastcore.xtras import modified_env


with modified_env(OLLAMA_HOST='localhost:11434'):
    test_eq(model_label('ollama/qwen3:8b'), 'a local model: Qwen 3 8B')
    test_eq(provider_label('ollama', ['ollama/qwen3:8b']), 'On this Mac (Ollama)')

With $OLLAMA_HOST on another computer, the model is not called local, and its group has a hosted name. The check reads only the host name: it does not connect:

with modified_env(OLLAMA_HOST='http://gpu-box.lan:11434'):
    test_eq(model_label('ollama/qwen3:8b'), 'Qwen 3 8B')
    test_eq(provider_label('ollama', ['ollama/qwen3:8b']), 'Ollama on another computer')

The other groups keep their names from PROVIDERS. A provider that is not in it gets its own name:

test_eq(provider_label('mlx', ['qwen-4b']), 'On this Mac (MLX)')
test_eq(provider_label('claude', ['claude/sonnet']), 'Claude')
test_eq(provider_label('groq'), 'Groq')
test_eq(provider_label(''), 'Other')


Where a model runs
where_of says where the model name runs: on this Mac or hosted, and the company of a hosted model. It uses _on_mac, as provider_label does, so an Ollama daemon on another computer is hosted. An unknown model is hosted, as the guard takes it. where_chip gives the short text for the page.


source

where_chip
def where_chip(
    name:str
)->str:
on this Mac, or hosted · <company>, for the model name.




source

where_of
def where_of(
    name:str
)->dict:
Who runs the model name: model (its label), where (on this Mac or hosted) and who (the company of a hosted model). An unknown model is hosted, as the guard takes it.


A Claude model is hosted by Anthropic. A model on an Ollama daemon on this Mac stays here.

test_eq(where_chip('claude/haiku'), 'hosted · Anthropic')
test_eq(where_chip('copilot/gpt-6-sol'), 'hosted · GitHub')
with modified_env(OLLAMA_HOST='localhost:11434'): test_eq(where_chip('ollama/qwen3:8b'), HERE)
with modified_env(OLLAMA_HOST='http://gpu-box.lan:11434'): test_eq(where_chip('ollama/qwen3:8b'), 'hosted · Ollama on another computer')
test_eq(where_of(''), dict(where='hosted'))

catalog lists the models that can run here, for the Settings page. With the models extra, the list is the full list of models. Each row gets a name from model_label. The list stays in memory for five minutes, because the look-up asks each provider. Without the extra, the list has only the models in FALLBACK.


source

catalog
def catalog(
    ttl:float=300.0
)->list:
The models that can run here, as dicts with value, name, label, provider and source.


Without the models extra, the list has the three Claude tiers, each with a name.

_cat.clear()
try: import ramabana; has_rama = True
except ImportError: has_rama = False
if not has_rama: test_eq([r['name'] for r in catalog()], ['Claude Sonnet', 'Claude Haiku', 'Claude Opus'])
assert all(r['name'] for r in catalog())



One row for each model
Some models come through two providers. For example, Claude Haiku 5.5 comes through Claude Code and through GitHub Copilot, and GPT-6.1 Sol through Codex, GitHub Copilot and the OpenAI API. Each route has its own id, so the list showed the same name two or three times. one_each keeps one row for each name: the route of the first provider in ramabana’s READY_ORDER (subscriptions first, then keys). The row keeps the other ids in also. A saved id (keep) always stays, so the list shows the choice that you made.


source

one_each
def one_each(
    rows:list, keep:str=''
)->list:
One row of rows for each model name, in the first place of that name: the saved id keep, else the route that ramabana tries first. also has the other ids. An alias with a version beside it goes into the also of the newest version.


Claude Haiku 5.5 shows one time, on Claude Code. With the Copilot id saved, the Copilot row stays.

dup = [dict(value='copilot/claude-haiku-5.5', name='Claude Haiku 5.5', provider='copilot'), dict(value='claude/sonnet', name='Claude Sonnet', provider='claude'),
       dict(value='claude/claude-haiku-5-5', name='Claude Haiku 5.5', provider='claude')]
test_eq([(r['value'], r['also']) for r in one_each(dup)], [('claude/claude-haiku-5-5', ['copilot/claude-haiku-5.5']), ('claude/sonnet', [])])
test_eq(one_each(dup, keep='copilot/claude-haiku-5.5')[0]['value'], 'copilot/claude-haiku-5.5')

An alias such as claude/opus and its version, such as Claude Opus 5.5, are one model. The list shows only the version, with the alias in also. A saved alias stays.

al = [dict(value='claude/opus', name='Claude Opus', provider='claude'), dict(value='claude/claude-opus-4-1', name='Claude Opus 4.1', provider='claude'),
      dict(value='claude/claude-opus-5-5', name='Claude Opus 5.5', provider='claude'), dict(value='codex/gpt-5', name='GPT-5', provider='codex'),
      dict(value='codex/gpt-5-mini', name='GPT-5 Mini', provider='codex')]
test_eq([(r['name'], r['also']) for r in one_each(al)], [('Claude Opus 4.1', []), ('Claude Opus 5.5', ['claude/opus']), ('GPT-5', []), ('GPT-5 Mini', [])])
test_eq([r['name'] for r in one_each(al, keep='claude/opus')][:2], ['Claude Opus', 'Claude Opus 4.1'])

Router is the ask the app gives the tutor. Called as it is, it uses the default model. for_(task) gives the ask for one task: the model the settings name for it, else the default. for_(task, name, job) gives the ask for task on the model name, on the ramabana job job. The Test button of the Settings page uses the job test:<task>, so a test does not move the job of the task. When the default routes by task, as RouteAsk below does, for_ lets it make the ask. cap(task) gives the reply cap of the task, read on each call. warm starts the backend of each task in the background.


source

for_task
def for_task(
    ask, task:str
):
The ask for task when ask routes by task, else ask itself.




source

Router
def Router(
    dflt, models:NoneType=None, tokens:NoneType=None
):
The tutor’s model: a default ask, and one model for each task that the settings name.


A router with no settings uses the default for every task. A task that names a model gets that model.

dflt = Fake(dflt='default')
r = Router(dflt, models=lambda: {})
test_eq(r('x'), 'default')
test_is(r.for_('grade'), dflt)
named = Fake(dflt='named'); named.model = 'fast'
_asks['fast'] = named
r = Router(dflt, models=lambda: dict(grade='fast'))
test_eq(r.for_('grade')('x'), 'named')
test_eq(r.for_('question')('x'), 'default')
test_is(for_task(dflt, 'grade'), dflt)

title: llm
text:
Every call through ramabana
ramabana is the agent layer on top of the model layer. Its Routing sends each job to a model. When a cloud model fails or gives no answer, Routing puts it aside for five minutes and sends the job to the next route: other cloud models, then a small model on this Mac. Its backends stay open, so a call does not pay the start time of a new Chat.
ramabana_agent makes one ramabana Agent for the process, on the first call. The Agent gets only what Agent.oneshot needs:

NullHost: no folders, and each file operation is refused.
readonly=True, no sub-agents, no extensions, no skills, no lessons: no tool can write, run code or go on the network.
Approvals that refuse when nobody answers, and no saved rules.
cfg=None: no history, plan or run log, so the Agent writes no files.
A short briefing, so that it does not read skills or project files.

The turn of the Agent is the default model, so a task whose model fails goes to the default model first.


source

ramabana_agent
def ramabana_agent(
    turn:str=None
):
The one ramabana Agent of this process, made on first use on the turn dflt_model(turn): no folders, no tool that acts, no files.


Each task is a ramabana job with the same name. _point sets the model of the job before each call, only when the settings changed it. A model that ramabana put aside stays aside until its time is up.
ramabana_oneshot asks one question on the job of a task. ramabana’s Backend.oneshot does not wait when another call holds the backend: it gives ’’. So the call holds the abhyasa lock of each backend that it uses. Agent.oneshot calls fits(b) just before it asks the backend b, on the first route and on each fallback. fits lets go of the lock of the route before, then waits for the lock of b. A call holds one lock at a time, so two calls cannot wait for each other. When no route gives an answer, the call raises.
A failure can take some time: ramabana tries each route in turn, then the small model on this Mac. It puts a failed cloud model aside for five minutes.
A route can also raise ramabana’s OneshotTimeout when a call goes past its deadline. timeout_error changes it into the same RuntimeError as a call with no answer. The error names the model and the seconds, so each caller catches one kind of error.
prepare lets the caller change the text for each route, as ramabana’s Agent.oneshot does. The guide uses it for its guard: the guard then knows if the model of the route is on this Mac. HOSTED is the model that a guard takes when it does not know the route.


source

ramabana_oneshot
def ramabana_oneshot(
    job:str, name:str, prompt:str, sp:str='', max_tokens:int=4096, prepare:NoneType=None
)->str:
Ask prompt on the ramabana job job, pointed at the model name. Wait for a busy backend. Raise when no route answers. prepare(prompt, sp, backend) gives the text for each route, so a guard knows the model that gets it.




source

timeout_error
def timeout_error(
    job:str, e, name:str=''
)->RuntimeError:
The RuntimeError for the ramabana OneshotTimeout e on the job job: it names the model (name, else the route of e) and the seconds.


ramabana_stream is the twin of ramabana_oneshot that gives the reply as the model sends it, through ramabana’s Agent.oneshot_stream. It holds the same lock of each backend, and it raises the same errors. The guard (prepare) runs before the stream starts. A route that cannot stream (ramabana’s StreamUnsupported, before it sends anything) gives the whole reply of ramabana_oneshot as one chunk, so the caller does not need a second path.


source

ramabana_stream
def ramabana_stream(
    job:str, name:str, prompt:str, sp:str='', max_tokens:int=4096, prepare:NoneType=None
):
The reply of ramabana_oneshot, one chunk at a time as the model sends it. A route that cannot stream gives the whole reply as one chunk. Raise when no route answers.


RouteAsk is the default ask of the web app. via(task, name, max_tokens) gives the ask of one task, and Router.for_ uses it. A call with no task goes to the job ask:<model>. warm starts the backend of each task, with no model call. route_ask gives a RouteAsk when ramabana is installed, else rishi_ask with a warning.


source

route_ask
def route_ask(
    model:str=None
):
The default ask: a RouteAsk when ramabana is installed, else rishi_ask.




source

RouteAsk
def RouteAsk(
    model:str=None
):
The default ask: each call goes through the routing of ramabana, on the job of its task.



The worker agent
ramabana_worker makes a second ramabana Agent, for the gather agent of research. It is never the one Agent of ramabana_agent, so a long gather never holds a one-shot call. It runs on the default routing (Routing(turn=dflt_model())). Its host is the shalya host (default: a NullHost, with no folders). The caller names its tools in tools, then adds them with add_tool. ramabana’s only_tools offers the model only those tools, and refuses a tool with another name. ramabana’s memory and plan tools are held back. It has no approvals listener, so a tool that writes is refused. The caps stop a turn after max_calls tool calls, max_steps model steps, max_tokens tokens or max_cost dollars. A model such as Claude Code on a plan reports no cost. Then ramabana estimates the dollars from the tokens at the price of the model (ramabana.agent.token_rate), and keeps the estimate in estimated, so the dollar cap still holds.


source

ramabana_lead
def ramabana_lead(
    read_roots:tuple=(), tools:list=(), sp:str='You are the source gatherer of abhyasa, a tutor.', turn:str=None,
    minutes:float=15, max_calls:int=300, max_steps:int=80, max_cost:float=5.0, max_tokens:int=2000000
)->tuple:
(agent, host): a new ramabana Agent made by ramabana’s mk_agent, with its own read and web tools (LEAD_TOOLS) and its sub-agents (delegate_search, at most 4 at once in the whole tree), on the turn dflt_model(turn). Its sub-agents run on ramabana’s subagent route. The folders read_roots are open for reads only; its one folder that it may write is a new empty one. It has no Python (python='off'), no vault, and no approvals listener, so each tool that writes is refused. The model sees only LEAD_TOOLS and the tools named in tools, when the caller adds them. The caps: max_calls tool calls in the whole tree, max_steps model steps, max_tokens tokens and max_cost dollars for a turn, and minutes for a sub-agent.




source

ramabana_worker
def ramabana_worker(
    tools:list=(), host:NoneType=None, sp:str='You are the source gatherer of abhyasa, a tutor.', turn:str=None,
    max_calls:int=300, max_steps:int=80, max_cost:float=5.0, max_tokens:int=2000000
):
A new ramabana Agent on the turn dflt_model(turn), with the shalya host (default: no folders). The model sees only the tools named in tools, when the caller adds them. Never the agent of ramabana_agent. A turn stops at max_tokens tokens, and at max_cost dollars (estimated from the tokens when the model reports no cost).


The worker offers only the tool that the test names and adds. It is a new Agent each time, and never the shared one. The caps reach the Agent.

if _has_ramabana():
    def look(q:str, # what to look for
             ) -> str:
        "Look for `q`."
        return q
    w = ramabana_worker(['look'], max_calls=50, max_tokens=1000)
    w.add_tool(look)
    test_eq([t.__name__ for t in w.tools], ['look'])
    assert w is not ramabana_worker() and w is not ramabana_agent()
    test_eq((w.readonly, w.subagents, w.tool_budget, w.max_cost, w.max_tokens), (True, False, 50, WORKER_DOLLARS, 1000))

The worker refuses a tool that tools does not name. A worker with no names offers no tool, so ramabana’s own tools stay out.

if _has_ramabana():
    def write(path:str, # the file
              ) -> str:
        "Write `path`."
        return path
    test_fail(lambda: w.add_tool(write), contains='not in only_tools')
    test_eq(ramabana_worker().tools, [])

When the model reports no cost, ramabana estimates the dollars from the tokens with its own price table (est_rate is None), and keeps them in estimated. A new worker has estimated nothing, and has the default token cap.

if _has_ramabana():
    w = ramabana_worker()
    test_eq((w.est_rate, w.estimated, w.max_tokens), (None, 0., WORKER_TOKENS))

The lead of research is made by ramabana’s mk_agent. It offers ramabana’s read and web tools and delegate_search, and the tool that the test adds. It has no tool that writes a file or runs a command. The folder of the learner is open for reads only.

if _has_ramabana():
    import tempfile, shutil


if _has_ramabana():
    ro = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    a, h = ramabana_lead([ro], ['look'], minutes=2)
    a.add_tool(look)
    names = {t.__name__ for t in a.tools}
    assert {'view_file', 'read_url', 'web_search', 'delegate_search', 'look'} <= names, names
    assert not names & {'run_shell', 'run_python', 'create_file', 'replace_text', 'git_commit', 'add_root'}, names
    test_eq((h.read_roots, a.subagent_timeout, a.subagent_writes), ([str(Path(ro).resolve())], 120, False))
    a.close(); shutil.rmtree(h.scratch, ignore_errors=True)



Tests of the route
These tests use a ramabana Agent with fake backends from ramabana.testing, so no model runs. using(a) puts that Agent in place of the real one for one test. CI does not install the models extra, so these tests run only when ramabana is installed.

from contextlib import contextmanager
from collections import Counter
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor


if has_rama:
    from ramabana.core import resolve
    from ramabana.testing import fake_agent, FakeBackend


@contextmanager
def using(a):
    "Use the `Agent` `a` in place of the real one, for one test."
    _ra['agent'] = a
    try: yield a
    finally: _ra.pop('agent', None)

Each task goes to the ramabana job with the same name. The task that the settings name gets its model, the other tasks get the default. Each call asks for the reply cap of its task, TOKENS[task], so a long question with its rubric is not cut.

if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    jobs, one = [], a.oneshot
    a.oneshot = lambda p, sp='', job='oneshot', max_tokens=None, fits=None: jobs.append((job, max_tokens)) or one(p, sp, job, max_tokens, fits)
    with using(a):
        r = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(grade='claude/haiku'), tokens=lambda: {})
        test_eq(r.for_('grade')('hi'), 'ONESHOT:hi')
        test_eq(r.for_('question').model, 'claude/sonnet')
        r.for_('question')('hi')
    test_eq(jobs, [('grade', TOKENS['grade']), ('question', TOKENS['question'])])
    test_eq((a.routing.policy['grade'], a.routing.policy['question']), ('claude/haiku', 'claude/sonnet'))

A change in the settings has an effect on the next call, with no restart. An empty choice goes back to the default.

if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    ms = dict(grade='claude/haiku')
    with using(a):
        r = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: ms)
        r.for_('grade')('hi'); test_eq(a.routing.policy['grade'], 'claude/haiku')
        ms['grade'] = 'claude/opus'; r.for_('grade')('hi'); test_eq(a.routing.policy['grade'], 'claude/opus')
        ms['grade'] = ''; r.for_('grade')('hi'); test_eq(a.routing.policy['grade'], 'claude/sonnet')

prepare gets each route. Here it writes the name of the model before the prompt, so the reply shows what the route got:

if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    with using(a): test_eq(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet').via('hint', prepare=lambda p, sp, b: (f'{b.spec.name} {p}', sp))('hi'), 'ONESHOT:fake hi')

Slow is a fake backend that takes a moment to answer. It sets inside when a call starts.

if has_rama:
    class Slow(FakeBackend):
        "A fake backend that answers after 0.2 s and sets `inside` when a call starts."
        def __init__(self, *a, **kw): super().__init__(*a, **kw); self.inside = threading.Event()
        def _oneshot(self, prompt, sp, max_tokens): self.inside.set(); time.sleep(0.2); return f'ONESHOT:{prompt}'

This is why the route has a lock. ramabana’s Agent.oneshot does not wait for a busy backend: a second call at the same time gets ’’.

if has_rama:
    a, _ = fake_agent(); slow = Slow(); a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': slow
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        f1 = ex.submit(a.oneshot, 'one'); slow.inside.wait(); f2 = ex.submit(a.oneshot, 'two')
    test_eq((f1.result(), f2.result()), ('ONESHOT:one', ''))

Through the route, the second call waits for the first, and both calls get an answer.

if has_rama:
    slow.inside.clear()
    with using(a), ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        ask = RouteAsk('claude/sonnet').via('question')
        f1 = ex.submit(ask, 'one'); slow.inside.wait(); f2 = ex.submit(ask, 'two')
        test_eq((f1.result(), f2.result()), ('ONESHOT:one', 'ONESHOT:two'))

When no route gives an answer, the call raises. The error names the task, the model and the note of ramabana, so ask_json never gets ’’.

if has_rama:
    class Empty(FakeBackend):
        "A fake cloud backend that answers nothing."
        def _oneshot(self, prompt, sp, max_tokens): return ''
    a, _ = fake_agent(); empty = Empty(resolve('claude/haiku')); a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': empty
    with using(a):
        ask = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(grade='claude/haiku')).for_('grade')
        test_fail(lambda: ask('hi'), contains='grade task')
        try: ask('hi')
        except RuntimeError as e: assert 'claude/haiku' in str(e) and 'answered nothing' in str(e), e

A route that goes past its deadline raises ramabana’s OneshotTimeout. The call raises the same RuntimeError, with the model and the seconds, and keeps the first error as its cause.

if has_rama:
    from ramabana.runtime import OneshotTimeout


if has_rama:
    a, _ = fake_agent()
    def late(*a, **kw): raise OneshotTimeout('claude/haiku', 31.6, True)
    a.oneshot = late
    with using(a):
        try: RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('grade')('hi'); assert False, 'no error'
        except RuntimeError as e:
            test_eq(str(e), 'The grade task got no answer from claude/haiku through ramabana: claude/haiku did not answer in 32 seconds.')
            assert isinstance(e.__cause__, OneshotTimeout)



Tests of the stream
Chunks is a fake backend that can stream: it sends its reply three letters at a time. ask.stream gives the chunks in order, and their join is the reply. The guard of prepare sees the route before the stream starts.

if has_rama:
    class Chunks(FakeBackend):
        "A fake backend that streams `ONESHOT:<prompt>` in chunks of 3 letters."
        supports_stream = True
        def _oneshot_stream(self, prompt, sp, max_tokens): return (f'ONESHOT:{prompt}'[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(f'ONESHOT:{prompt}'), 3))
    a, _ = fake_agent(); ch = Chunks(resolve('claude/haiku')); a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': ch
    with using(a): got = list(RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('hint', prepare=lambda p, sp, b: (f'{b.spec.name} {p}', sp)).stream('hi'))
    test_eq(''.join(got), 'ONESHOT:claude/haiku hi')
    assert len(got) > 1

A backend that cannot stream (the default of FakeBackend) gives the whole reply of the blocking call as one chunk:

if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    with using(a): test_eq(list(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet').via('hint').stream('hi')), ['ONESHOT:hi'])

The stream lets go of the lock of its backend at the end, so the next call on that backend does not wait:

if has_rama:
    a, _ = fake_agent(); a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': ch
    with using(a):
        list(RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('hint').stream('one'))
        assert _lock(ch).acquire(timeout=1); _lock(ch).release()
        it = RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('hint').stream('two'); next(it); it.close()   # a stream that stops early lets go too
        assert _lock(ch).acquire(timeout=1); _lock(ch).release()

A stream with no text raises the same error as a blocking call, and a timeout raises the same RuntimeError:

if has_rama:
    a, _ = fake_agent(); empty = Empty(resolve('claude/haiku')); empty.supports_stream = True
    empty._oneshot_stream = lambda prompt, sp, max_tokens: (c for c in ())
    a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': empty
    with using(a): test_fail(lambda: list(RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('grade').stream('hi')), contains='grade task')
    def late(*a, **kw): raise OneshotTimeout('claude/haiku', 31.6, True); yield
    a.oneshot_stream = late
    with using(a): test_fail(lambda: list(RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('grade').stream('hi')), contains='did not answer in 32 seconds')

The next tests need ramabana’s real Routing, so that a failed model goes to its next route. routed_agent gives a fake Agent with the real Routing on two fake models: fake-main, the default, and fake-quick. They are hosted models with a fake key, so Routing takes them on any machine. make(spec) gives the fake backend of each model, and bes keeps them by name.

if has_rama:
    from ramabana.core import register_model, Routing


if has_rama:
    os.environ['ABHYASA_FAKE_KEY'] = 'not a real key'
    for n in ('fake-main', 'fake-quick'): register_model(n, f'fakevendor/{n}', runtime='remote', api_key_env='ABHYASA_FAKE_KEY')

    def routed_agent(make):
        "A fake `Agent` on the real `Routing`, with the turn on `fake-main`. Returns the `Agent` and the backends by model name."
        a, _ = fake_agent(routing=Routing(turn='fake-main'))
        del a._be_or_none   # the real one, which asks `Routing`
        bes = {}
        def be(job='turn'):
            s = a.routing.spec(job)
            if s.name not in bes: bes[s.name] = make(s)
            return bes[s.name]
        a._be = be
        return a, bes

A fallback holds the lock of the backend that it goes to. Here fake-quick answers nothing, so the grade call goes to fake-main. A question call on fake-main starts while that fallback runs. It waits for the lock, and both calls get an answer.

if has_rama:
    a, bes = routed_agent(lambda s: Slow(s) if s.name != 'fake-quick' else Empty(s))
    with using(a), ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        g = ex.submit(Router(RouteAsk('fake-main'), models=lambda: dict(grade='fake-quick'), tokens=lambda: {}).for_('grade'), 'g')
        while 'fake-main' not in bes: time.sleep(0.01)
        bes['fake-main'].inside.wait()
        q = ex.submit(RouteAsk('fake-main').via('question'), 'q')
        test_eq((g.result(), q.result()), ('ONESHOT:g', 'ONESHOT:q'))

When no route answers, each route is tried one time. The last route is the small model on this Mac, gemma-e4b.

if has_rama:
    calls = Counter()
    class Counted(Empty):
        "A fake backend that answers nothing and counts its calls."
        def _oneshot(self, prompt, sp, max_tokens): calls[self.spec.name] += 1; return ''
    a, bes = routed_agent(Counted)
    with using(a): test_fail(lambda: RouteAsk('fake-main').via('grade', 'fake-quick')('hi'), contains='grade task')
    test_eq(calls['gemma-e4b'], 1)
    test_eq(set(calls.values()), {1})

warm asks ramabana for the backend of each task in the background, and sends nothing to the model. It gives the thread. The jobs of WARM start too: the guide job, on the model of the screen guide (the model for hints when it has none). warm(['guide']) starts only the guide.

if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent(); seen = []
    a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': seen.append(job) or be
    with using(a):
        Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: {}).warm().join()
    test_eq(seen, [*TASKS, 'guide'])
    test_eq(be.sent, [])
    seen.clear()
    with using(a): Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(hint='claude/haiku')).warm(['guide']).join()
    test_eq((seen, a.routing.policy['guide']), (['guide'], 'claude/haiku'))
    with using(a): Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(hint='claude/haiku', guide='claude/opus')).warm(['guide']).join()
    test_eq(a.routing.policy['guide'], 'claude/opus')   # a model of its own wins

With ramabana, route_ask gives a RouteAsk. Without it, route_ask gives rishi_ask and a warning that says so one time.

import sys, warnings
from unittest.mock import patch


if has_rama: assert isinstance(route_ask(), RouteAsk)
with patch.dict(sys.modules, {'ramabana': None}), warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    ask = route_ask('claude/haiku')
test_eq(ask.model, 'claude/haiku')
assert not isinstance(ask, RouteAsk) and 'ramabana' in str(w[0].message)



The reply cap of each task
A reply cap comes from the settings table (tokens.<task>), from 1 to TOKENS_MAX. A cap that you typed in the file as text, such as "900", works too.

from abhyasa.settings import update_settings, val


update_settings('tokens', hint=' 900 ')
test_eq(val('tokens.hint'), 900)
update_settings('tokens', hint=str(TOKENS_MAX + 1))
test_eq(val('tokens.hint'), TOKENS_MAX)   # clamped to the top
update_settings('tokens', hint=None)

Router.cap gives the saved cap of a task, else the default of the task. A bad value in the settings file gives the default, so a call never fails because of it.

caps = dict(hint=300)
r = Router(Fake(), models=lambda: {}, tokens=lambda: caps)
test_eq(r.cap('hint'), 300)
test_eq(r.cap('grade'), TOKENS['grade'])
caps['hint'] = 'lots'; test_eq(r.cap('hint'), TOKENS['hint'])
caps['hint'] = 99999; test_eq(r.cap('hint'), TOKENS_MAX)          # out of range: the most

A task after extract (plan, pick, note, profile) borrows the model, the reply cap and the job of an older task until it has a model of its own.

class Via:
    model = 'base'
    def __call__(self, p, sp=''): return ''
    def via(self, job, name='', cap=None): return (job, name, cap)
ms = dict(extract='x/extract', hint='x/hint')
r = Router(Via(), models=lambda: ms, tokens=lambda: {})
test_eq((r.for_('plan'), r.for_('note')), (('extract', 'x/extract', 4096), ('hint', 'x/hint', 512)))
ms['plan'] = 'x/plan'
test_eq(r.for_('plan'), ('plan', 'x/plan', 4096))

The cap reaches Agent.oneshot, and a change has an effect on the next call.

if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    jobs, one = [], a.oneshot
    a.oneshot = lambda p, sp='', job='oneshot', max_tokens=None, fits=None: jobs.append((job, max_tokens)) or one(p, sp, job, max_tokens, fits)
    caps = dict(grade=777)
    with using(a):
        r = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: {}, tokens=lambda: caps)
        r.for_('grade')('hi'); caps['grade'] = ''; r.for_('grade')('hi')
    test_eq(jobs, [('grade', 777), ('grade', TOKENS['grade'])])

The Test button of the Settings page asks on its own job, test:<task>, with the cap of the task. The job of the task stays where the settings put it.

if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    jobs, one = [], a.oneshot
    a.oneshot = lambda p, sp='', job='oneshot', max_tokens=None, fits=None: jobs.append((job, max_tokens)) or one(p, sp, job, max_tokens, fits)
    with using(a):
        r = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(grade='claude/haiku'), tokens=lambda: {})
        r.for_('grade')('hi')
        r.for_('grade', 'claude/opus', job='test:grade')('hi')
    test_eq(jobs, [('grade', TOKENS['grade']), ('test:grade', TOKENS['grade'])])
    test_eq((a.routing.policy['grade'], a.routing.policy['test:grade']), ('claude/haiku', 'claude/opus'))

title: method
text:
Each question, hint and lesson uses one way to teach: its method. The tutor picks the method before it writes the prompt. So the tag is known, not guessed. When a question closes, its outcome counts for its method: solid 1, shaky 0.5, a miss 0.
The counts give each method a Beta posterior, for each subject and over all subjects. choose uses them in two ways:
The counts are in one stats document on the shelf. This document is only a cache: method_stats builds it again from the attempts.
Import the modules that this notebook uses.

title: method
text:
The methods
METHODS maps each method to the line that the prompt gets. EXAMPLES_TO maps the profile’s “examples that help” to methods, to set the prior.
The text of each method is a prompt that you can change in Settings (see prompts). way gives the text in use: your saved text, else the line in METHODS.


source

way
def way(
    m:str
)->str:
The text of method m now: your saved text, else the line in METHODS; ’’ for an unknown method.


With no saved text, way gives the line in METHODS.

test_eq([way(m) for m in METHODS], list(METHODS.values()))
test_eq(way('nope'), '')

title: method
text:
The stats document
stats reads the stats document. It gives empty counts when there is no document. set_stats writes the document. A lock makes sure that two closes at the same time do not lose a count.


source

Learning.set_stats
def set_stats(
    **kv
):
Change fields of the stats document.




source

Learning.stats
def stats()->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
The cached stats: method counts for each subject (* is all), recent credits, and calibration.

title: method
text:
Credit
credit adds one outcome to the counts and returns the new stats. It keeps the last 8 credits of each method, to find a method that gets better.


source

Learning.credit_method
def credit_method(
    method:str, subject:str, kind:str, w:float=1.0
):
Count outcome kind for method with the weight w in the stats document.




source

credit
def credit(
    st, method:str, subject:str, kind:str, w:float=1.0
)->dict:
The stats st with one outcome kind added for method with the weight w, in subject and in *. Only a full outcome (w=1) goes in the recent credits.


Solid adds 1 to a. A miss adds 1 to b. Shaky adds half to each. An unknown outcome or method changes nothing.

st = credit(credit(credit(EMPTY, 'code', 'ml', 'solid'), 'code', 'ml', 'fragile'), 'maths', 'ml', 'gap')
test_eq(st['methods']['ml'], {'code': [1.5, .5], 'maths': [0., 1.]})
test_eq(st['methods']['*'], st['methods']['ml'])
test_eq(st['recent'], {'code': [1., .5], 'maths': [0.]})
test_eq(credit(st, 'code', 'ml', 'closed'), st)


Feedback counts a little
The row under a demo or a lesson also counts for the way of that demo or lesson, with a small weight from FEEDBACK. “Not clear” adds 0.25 of a miss, so four of them count as one miss, and one click does not decide the way. “Just right” adds 0.1 of a pass. “Too simple” adds nothing: the way worked, but the step was too small. A part of an outcome does not go in the recent credits, so it does not make a way look better lately.

st = credit(EMPTY, 'analogy', 'ml', *FEEDBACK['unclear'])
test_eq(st['methods']['ml']['analogy'], [0., .25])
test_eq(st['recent'], {})
test_eq(credit(st, 'analogy', 'ml', *FEEDBACK['right'])['methods']['ml']['analogy'], [.1, .25])

title: method
text:
The posterior
posterior gives (a, b) for a method: Beta(1, 1), plus 2 on a for a method in the profile’s examples. For a subject, it adds the subject counts and the * counts. It scales the * counts down to at most 4 pseudo-counts. So a new subject starts from what works for you in other subjects.


source

improving
def improving(
    st, m:str
)->tuple | None:
(right, n) over the last 5 credits of m, when they are at least 0.2 above its mean over all; else None.




source

mean
def mean(
    ab
)->float:




source

posterior
def posterior(
    st, m:str, subject:str='', prior:tuple=()
)->tuple:
The Beta (a, b) of method m in subject.


With no counts, the prior decides. improving finds a method that got better recently.

test_eq(posterior(EMPTY, 'code'), (1., 1.))
test_eq(posterior(EMPTY, 'code', prior=['code']), (3., 1.))
gm = dict(methods={'*': {'maths': [2., 4.]}}, recent={'maths': [0., 0., 1., 1., 1., 1.]})
test_eq(improving(gm, 'maths'), (4, 5))
test_is(improving(dict(gm, recent={'maths': [1., 0., 0., 0.]}), 'maths'), None)

title: method
text:
Choose a method
choose returns (method, note). The note goes in the line that says why you get this question.


source

choose
def choose(
    st, subject:str='', weak:bool=False, rng:NoneType=None, explore:str='sometimes', prior:tuple=(),
    allowed:NoneType=None
)->tuple:
The method for the next question, and a note on why, from the allowed ways (default TEXT_WAYS). A weak concept gets the best method; else, sometimes, another one.


A weak concept gets the best method. With explore='never', choose always gives the best method. With sometimes, it tries a method that got better at times. It still gives the best method most of the time.

cs = dict(methods={'*': {'code': [7., 2.], 'maths': [2., 4.]}}, recent={'maths': [0., 0., 1., 1., 1., 1.]})
m, note = choose(cs, 'ml', weak=True)
test_eq(m, 'code'); assert note.startswith('drill with code: 7 of 9')
test_eq({choose(cs, 'ml', rng=random.Random(i), explore='never')[0] for i in range(30)}, {'code'})
picks = [choose(cs, 'ml', rng=random.Random(i)) for i in range(60)]
assert any(n.startswith('trying maths: you got better') for _, n in picks)
test_eq(sum(m == 'code' for m, _ in picks) > 30, True)   # with `sometimes`, the best method still comes most of the time

title: method
text:
The ways that fit
A session cannot show every way. choose takes allowed: the ways it may pick from. The default is TEXT_WAYS, the ways that every session can show. A list with no known way gives TEXT_WAYS too.

rng = random.Random(0)
assert {'demo', 'order', 'playground', 'board', 'timeline'} <= set(METHODS) and 'way.timeline' in PROMPTS
assert all(choose(EMPTY, rng=rng)[0] in TEXT_WAYS for _ in range(200))          # a session never gets a way it cannot show
assert all(choose(EMPTY, rng=rng, allowed=['demo', 'maths'])[0] in ('demo', 'maths') for _ in range(200))
assert choose(EMPTY, rng=rng, allowed=['board'])[0] in METHODS                   # an allowed list keeps its own ways
assert choose(EMPTY, rng=rng, allowed=['nope'])[0] in TEXT_WAYS                  # no known way: back to the text ways

title: method
text:
The way for a check
check_for picks the way for one check of one idea. It looks only at the ways of the idea that a walk can show. It does not repeat the way of the last check when it has another. The kind of the check follows the way, and the depth follows the kind.
A hands-on way of the idea (a key of CHECK_KIND: demo, order or code) comes before its text ways. The model lists a hands-on way only for an idea that fits it: a process, a sequence, or code. A code check is a notebook that runs in Leela. Without this rule, the learner stats and the profile pick a text way almost every time, because the profile names only text ways. Then nearly every check is a short answer.
Only the idea’s own ways can give a hands-on check. An idea with no way that a walk can show gets a short answer in a text way. A walk passes hands=False when it has its share of hands-on checks (see hands_most in journey).


source

check_for
def check_for(
    c, st, rng:NoneType=None, explore:str='sometimes', prior:tuple=(), last:str='', hands:bool=True
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
The way, kind, depth and reason for one check of concept c. A hands-on way of the idea comes before its text ways; hands=False leaves the hands-on ways out.


A check takes a way of its idea. An idea with no way that a walk can show gets a text way.

c = AttrDict(ways=['code', 'maths'], floor=0)
k = check_for(c, EMPTY, rng=random.Random(1))
assert (k.way, k.kind, k.depth) in {('code', 'notebook', 4), ('maths', 'short', 2)} and k.why
assert check_for(AttrDict(ways=['demo'], floor=0), EMPTY).kind == 'demo'
assert check_for(AttrDict(ways=['timeline'], floor=3), EMPTY).way in TEXT_WAYS   # no timeline view yet
assert check_for(AttrDict(ways=['words'], floor=3), EMPTY).depth == 3
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['demo', 'code'], floor=0), EMPTY, rng=rng, last='demo').way == 'code' for _ in range(20))

An idea that lists a hands-on way (demo, order or code) gets a check of that kind. This is true when a text way comes first in the list, and when the profile likes a text way. An idea with only text ways still gets a short answer.

assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['words', 'example', 'order'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k), prior=['example']).kind == 'order' for k in range(50))
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['maths', 'demo'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k)).kind == 'demo' for k in range(50))
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['words', 'analogy'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k)).kind == 'short' for k in range(50))

An idea with no ways, or with no way that a walk can show, gets a short answer, never a code check. With hands=False (the walk has its share of hands-on checks), an idea gets a short answer in one of its text ways, else in any text way.

assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=w, floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k)).kind == 'short' for w in ([], None, ['timeline']) for k in range(50))
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['code', 'maths'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k), hands=False).way == 'maths' for k in range(20))
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['demo'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k), hands=False).kind == 'short' for k in range(20))

title: method
section: In plain words, and from the attempts
text:
In plain words, and from the attempts
methods_text says what works, for a prompt and for the page. method_stats builds the counts again from the attempts, in order.


source

Learning.method_stats
def method_stats(
    n:int=2000
)->dict:
Count every final attempt with a method again, oldest first, with the feedback on each attempt, and save the counts. Return the stats.




source

methods_text
def methods_text(
    st, subject:str='', n:int=3
)->str:
The methods with counts, best first, as one line; empty when nothing is counted.


The counts that credit_method keeps match a rebuild from the attempts.

ml_ = temp_learning(); ml_.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
for m, k in (('code', 'solid'), ('code', 'fragile'), ('maths', 'gap')):
    ml_.record('ranking', f'{m} {k}?', final=True, method=m, outcome=k); ml_.credit_method(m, 'ml', k); time.sleep(.01)
inc = ml_.stats()
test_eq(ml_.method_stats()['methods'], inc.methods)
assert methods_text(inc, 'ml').startswith('Ways that work for you: code 2 of 2')

title: profile
text:
The tutor asks better questions when it knows the learner. A coder gets code examples. A Sanskrit reader gets a Sanskrit example. This module keeps one profile document on the learning shelf. The profile gets data in three ways: a short first conversation, edits by the learner, and changes that the tutor makes from evidence. The module keeps each change with who made it and why. So the learner can see each change and undo it. The profile stays in the vault on this machine.
Import the modules that this notebook uses.

title: profile
text:
The fields
A field is a list of short items, or one value. PACES names the three paces. EXAMPLES names the kinds of example a learner can like.
profile_text gives the profile as lines for a prompt. It is empty when the profile has no data. So the prompt for a new learner does not change.


source

profile_text
def profile_text(
    p
)->str:
The profile as prompt lines; empty when nothing is known.


clean makes a value fit its field. A list field takes a list or lines of text. The pace must be a known pace. The session length stays between 3 and 40.


source

clean
def clean(
    k, v
):
The value v made to fit field k.

title: profile
text:
The document
profile reads the document. It uses the defaults for the fields that are not set. known is False until the profile has a saved value.


source

Learning.profile
def profile()->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
The learner profile, with its list of changes, newest first.


set_profile changes fields. It keeps each change with the old value, the new value, who made it (you, onboarding or tutor) and why.


source

Learning.set_profile
def set_profile(
    by:str='you', why:str='', **kv
)->list:
Change fields of the profile and keep each change with who made it and why. Return the changes.


undo_profile puts back the old value of one change. It finds the change by its id. Two changes in one save can have the same time, so the time can not tell them apart. A change from before the ids has none, so for it the exact time is used. The undo is a change too, so the list shows all the changes.


source

Learning.clear_profile
def clear_profile():
Remove the profile and its changes.




source

Learning.undo_profile
def undo_profile(
    ref
)->list:
Put back the old value of the change ref: its id, or for an older change with no id, its exact time at.

title: profile
text:
The first conversation
The learner answers four questions, by voice or by text. One model call turns the answers into fields.


source

onboard
def onboard(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, answers:dict
)->list:
Fill the profile from the onboarding answers. Return the changes.




source

onboard_prompt
def onboard_prompt(
    answers:dict
)->str:
The prompt that turns the onboarding answers into profile fields.

title: profile
text:
The tutor learns from evidence
observe reads the recent answers: right or not, confidence, hints, misconceptions and think-aloud. A small model call proposes at most three changes, each with its reason. observe applies them immediately and keeps each one with its reason. So the learner sees them and can undo them.


source

observe_prompt
def observe_prompt(
    p, ev:str, st:NoneType=None
)->str:
The prompt that proposes changes to profile p from the evidence ev and the method counts in the stats st.




source

evidence
def evidence(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, n:int=12
)->str:
The last n final answers as short lines for a prompt: the outcome, the method, the first error, gaps you named, lessons you asked for, and what you said.


observe applies the changes. A list field takes add and remove. The pace takes value. The goals and the notes are for the learner only, so observe drops a change to them.


source

observe
def observe(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, n:int=12
)->list:
Change the profile from the recent answers. Return the changes, each with its reason.

title: profile
section: How well you know what you know
text:
How well you know what you know
A good learner knows what they know. When you feel sure and you are often wrong, you stop checking your own thinking. When you feel unsure and you are often right, you hold back ideas that work. The “Sure?” choice on each answer gives the data. calibration counts the first try of each question. It counts how many times you felt sure (60% or more), and how many of those answers were right. It counts the same for unsure. An answer with no confidence, a “don’t know” and a demo do not count.


source

calibration
def calibration(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, n:int=300
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
How often the first try of a question was right, when you felt sure and when you felt unsure.


calibration_text gives the calibration in plain words, with one line about what it means. With fewer than five answers, it gives an empty text.


source

calibration_text
def calibration_text(
    r
)->str:
The calibration r in plain words; empty with fewer than five answers.

title: profile
text:
Tests
A new shelf has an empty profile, and its prompt text is empty.

from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
from abhyasa.llm import Fake


lr = temp_learning()
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.known, p.pace, p.background, profile_text(p)), (False, 'steady', [], ''))

set_profile keeps each change, with who made it. Lines of text become a list.

ch = lr.set_profile(background='codes in Python\nknows Sanskrit grammar', pace='gentle')
test_eq([c['field'] for c in ch], ['background', 'pace'])
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.known, p.background, p.changes[0]['by']), (True, ['codes in Python', 'knows Sanskrit grammar'], 'you'))
assert 'Background: codes in Python; knows Sanskrit grammar' in profile_text(p) and 'Pace: gentle' in profile_text(p)

When a value stays the same, set_profile makes no change. A bad pace becomes steady, and the session length stays in its range.

test_eq(lr.set_profile(pace='gentle'), [])
test_eq((clean('pace', 'warp'), clean('session_len', '200'), clean('session_len', 'x')), ('steady', 40, 12))

undo_profile puts back the old value, and keeps the undo as a change.

cid = [c for c in lr.profile().changes if c['field'] == 'pace'][0]['id']
lr.undo_profile(cid)
test_eq((lr.profile().pace, lr.profile().changes[0]['why']), ('steady', 'you undid a change'))

Two changes in one save can have the same time. Each change has its own id, so the undo changes only the one that you pick.

import time as _t


real = _t.time
_t.time = lambda: 1000.0   # every change of this save gets the same time
try: lr.set_profile(pace='fast', session_len=20)
finally: _t.time = real
two = lr.profile().changes[:2]
test_eq(two[0]['at'], two[1]['at'])
lr.undo_profile([c for c in two if c['field'] == 'pace'][0]['id'])
test_eq((lr.profile().pace, lr.profile().session_len), ('steady', 20))

onboard fills fields from the answers with one model call.

fake = Fake({'make a short learner profile': dict(goals=['understand LLM papers'], examples=['code', 'maths'], session_len=8, pace='steady', notes='')})
ch = onboard(lr, fake, dict(want='LLMs, to read papers', how='code please'))
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.goals, p.examples, p.session_len), (['understand LLM papers'], ['code', 'maths'], 8))
test_eq({c['by'] for c in ch}, {'onboarding'})

observe changes the profile from attempts and keeps the reason. It drops a change to a field that it must not change.

lr.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml')
lr.record('attention', 'What shape is QK^T?', answer='d by d', correct=False, confidence=80, depth=3, misconception='mixes up the axes', final=True)
fake.rules['You keep a short profile'] = dict(changes=[dict(field='confuses', add='tensor shapes in attention', why='You missed a shape question with high confidence.'),
                                                     dict(field='goals', add='hack the planet', why='no')])
ch = observe(lr, fake)
test_eq([c['field'] for c in ch], ['confuses'])
test_eq((lr.profile().confuses, lr.profile().changes[0]['by']), (['tensor shapes in attention'], 'tutor'))
assert 'misconception: mixes up the axes' in fake.calls[-1][0]

With no answers there is no evidence, and no model call.

n = len(fake.calls)
test_eq(observe(temp_learning(), fake), [])
test_eq(len(fake.calls), n)

calibration counts the first try of each question. A pass after a wrong try counts as wrong. A “don’t know” and an answer with no confidence do not count.

kl = temp_learning(); kl.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml')
def rec(q, ok, conf, **kw): kl.record('attention', q, correct=ok, confidence=conf, session='s1', **kw)
rec('q1', False, 90, final=False); rec('q1', True, 90, final=True)   # sure, but wrong on the first try
rec('q2', True, 90); rec('q3', True, 30); rec('q4', False, 10)
rec('q5', False, None, dont_know=True); rec('q6', True, None)
test_eq(calibration(kl), dict(sure=2, sure_right=1, unsure=2, unsure_right=1))
test_eq(calibration_text(calibration(kl)), '')                       # four answers: too few to say

With enough answers, the text gives the counts and one line about what they mean.

test_eq(calibration_text(AttrDict(sure=4, sure_right=1, unsure=1, unsure_right=0)),
        'When you felt sure, you were right in 1 of 4. When you felt unsure, you were right in 0 of 1. '
        'You are often sure and wrong. Before you answer, ask: how could this be wrong?')
assert calibration_text(AttrDict(sure=1, sure_right=1, unsure=4, unsure_right=4)).endswith('Trust your first idea a little more.')

evidence reads the full conversation of a question. It gets the first error from a nudge, and the ideas that you said you did not know. It also gets a lesson that you asked for, the method, and each thing you said.

el = temp_learning(); el.put('Neuron', 'z = w . x + b.', 'ml')
th = [dict(who='you', text="I don't know what the loop means"), dict(who='tutor', kind='nudge', text='A loop adds products.', first_error='You use squares.'),
      dict(who='you', text='2(w1x1 + w2x2 + b)')]
el.record('neuron', 'Why does z double?', answer='2z', final=True, outcome='fragile', method='maths', thread=th, gaps=['weighted sum as a loop'], taught=1, teach_method='code')
ev = evidence(el)
for s in ('taught with maths', 'first error: You use squares.', 'said they did not know: weighted sum as a loop', 'asked for a lesson after it (code)', "I don't know what the loop means / 2(w1x1"):
    assert s in ev, s

observe keeps the calibration in the stats document. So each new question can read it, and does not have to read all attempts.

observe(el, Fake({'keep a short profile': dict(changes=[])}))
test_eq(set(el.stats().calib), {'sure', 'sure_right', 'unsure', 'unsure_right'})
test_eq((clean('explore', 'often'), clean('explore', 'always')), ('often', 'sometimes'))

clear_profile removes the full profile and its list of changes.

lr.clear_profile()
test_eq((lr.profile().known, lr.profile().changes), (False, []))

title: voice
text:
This module turns a spoken answer into text. With the local engines, the audio does not go off the machine. The web app records while you talk. It cuts the audio into segments at your pauses and sends each segment here. This module transcribes the segments one at a time, in order. The text goes into the think-aloud box while you continue to talk.
The module also speaks. speak turns one line of the screen guide into WAV audio, with the start time of each word, so the board can light each word as it is said.
These are the imports of the module.

title: voice
text:
Engines
There are two engines. mlx runs on this machine. openai sends the audio to OpenAI.

mlx runs any speech to text model that mlx-audio can load. The default is Qwen3-ASR 0.6B (8 bit, 1.0 GB). Whisper large-v3-turbo is the second model on the Settings page, and the search finds the others. Install mlx-audio with pip install abhyasa[whisper].
openai uses the OpenAI transcription API. It is off until you set a key. It sends the audio off the machine.

Each engine gets a hint: the name of the concept and its terms. Qwen3-ASR reads it as hot words, Whisper as its initial prompt, and OpenAI as its prompt.
The table gives the numbers on this machine (an M-series Mac), with each model warm. “Clip A” is the English test clip of the model layer (rishi/nbs/speech.wav). “Clip B” is a clip in a cloned voice with Nyāya terms in IAST and technical terms. “Terms” is the fraction of the 9 key terms in clip B that the engine wrote correctly. “5 s” is the time for one 5-second segment.
