“load” is a cold start of a cached model in a new process, with the Python imports. The first download takes longer.
“memory” is the MLX peak.
“Sanskrit CER” is the character error rate on a 9-second Nyāya sūtra (from vachaka), after the vachaka normalization.
Moonshine gave no text for the 24-second clip A. It is good only for short segments.
For Sanskrit speech, use Qwen3-ASR or Whisper with the hint, or vachaka.

Qwen3-ASR 0.6B is the default. With the hint, it has no errors on clip B and it writes all 9 terms. One 5-second segment takes 0.14 s. Before 0.0.16, the default was Gemma 4 E4B on LiteRT. It had the same score, but it was 5 times slower, and its model was 3.7 GB.
DFLT_STT is the default model of the mlx engine. The other constants are the named models. ALIASES keeps the old engine names: whisper and parakeet are the mlx engine with a fixed model. gemma was the default engine before 0.0.16, so it becomes the mlx engine with the default model. POCKET is the Hugging Face repo of the local voice (see “A natural voice” below), and POCKET_FILES are the files of its English model and of its default voice. The repo has many languages, so abhyasa gets only these files.

title: voice
text:
Settings
The settings are in settings.json in cfg_dir(). The settings module keeps the table of values and the file; this module uses its stt section. The web app changes the settings, and the next segment uses the change. You do not have to restart.
Without a file, you get the defaults. A change to one key keeps the other keys.

test_eq({k: settings()['stt'][k] for k in ('engine', 'model', 'segment')}, dict(engine='mlx', model='', segment=True))
update_settings('stt', segment=False)
test_eq(val('stt.segment'), False)
update_settings('stt', segment=True)

current gives the engine and model in use. $ABHYASA_STT has priority over the settings. It can be an engine (mlx), an old name (whisper, gemma), or an engine and a model (mlx:mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo-asr-fp16). An old settings file with gemma and a LiteRT model gets the default model. Nothing writes the file again.


source

current
def current()->tuple:
The engine and model in use: $ABHYASA_STT, else the settings.




source

resolve
def resolve(
    engine:str, model:str=''
)->tuple:
The engine and model for a name: aliases become mlx, engine:model splits, an empty model gets the default.


The settings give Qwen3-ASR by default. An old gemma setting gives the same, also with its old model. The environment variable has priority.

test_eq(current(), ('mlx', DFLT_STT))
test_eq(resolve('gemma', 'litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm'), ('mlx', DFLT_STT))
test_eq(resolve('parakeet'), ('mlx', DFLT_PARAKEET))
test_eq(resolve('mlx:mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16'), ('mlx', 'mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16'))
test_fail(lambda: resolve('kokoro'), contains='unknown')
os.environ['ABHYASA_STT'] = 'whisper'
test_eq(current(), ('mlx', DFLT_WHISPER))
os.environ['ABHYASA_STT'] = 'gemma'
test_eq(current(), ('mlx', DFLT_STT))
del os.environ['ABHYASA_STT']

title: voice
text:
One model in memory
resident keeps one model loaded in each slot: stt for speech to text, tts for the speaking voice. When the app asks for a different model in a slot, it frees the old model of that slot first. Two large models for the same job in memory at the same time can make the Mac slow.


source

resident
def resident(
    key, load, close:NoneType=None, slot:str='stt'
):
The loaded model of slot for key: when key is new, free the old model of the slot, then load() the new one.




source

unload
def unload(
    slot:str='stt'
):
Free the loaded model of slot: stt (speech to text) or tts (the speaking voice).


A new key frees the old model. The same key does not load again. A model in the tts slot does not free the model in the stt slot.

freed = []
resident('a', lambda: 'A', freed.append)
test_eq(resident('a', lambda: 'other'), 'A')
test_eq(resident('b', lambda: 'B'), 'B')
test_eq(freed, ['A'])
test_eq(resident('k', lambda: 'K', slot='tts'), 'K')
test_eq((resident('b', lambda: 'other'), freed), ('B', ['A']))
unload(); unload('tts')

Each engine is a function that takes a WAV path, a hint and a model, and returns text.
The mlx engine gives the hint to a model that accepts one: Whisper as initial_prompt, Qwen3-ASR as hotwords.
A Whisper-like model gets initial_prompt. A Qwen3-like model gets a list of hot words. A model without either gets nothing.

class _W:
    def generate(self, audio, initial_prompt=None): pass
class _Q:
    def generate(self, audio, hotwords=None): pass
test_eq(_hint_kw(_W(), 'Nyāya, hetu'), dict(initial_prompt='Nyāya, hetu'))
test_eq(_hint_kw(_Q(), 'Nyāya, hetu'), dict(hotwords=['Nyāya', 'hetu']))
test_eq(_hint_kw(_W(), ''), {})

title: voice
text:
OpenAI
The openai engine posts the WAV to the OpenAI transcription API, with the hint as its prompt. http_post is httpx.post unless a test puts a fake in its place.
The key comes from the first of these places that has OPENAI_API_KEY: the environment, the abhyasa keys.env, then the ramabana keys.env. ramabana says where its file is ($RAMABANA_CONFIG, else ~/.config/ramabana/keys.env). abhyasa reads both files with ramabana’s load_keys. It refuses a file that other users can read, and it runs !command values. abhyasa only reads the ramabana file. set_openai_key writes the abhyasa file with save_key (atomic, mode 0600). ramabana is an optional extra. Without it, abhyasa reads and writes plain NAME=value lines. masked shows only the last 4 characters.


source

masked
def masked(
    key:str
)->str:




source

set_openai_key
def set_openai_key(
    key:str=''
):
Save key in abhyasa’s keys.env (mode 0600); an empty key clears it. A key with other than letters, digits, - and _ raises ValueError.




source

openai_key
def openai_key()->tuple:
The OpenAI key and where it is from; ('', '') when there is none.


A key in the abhyasa file comes back with its source, and the file has mode 0600. When the abhyasa file has no key, abhyasa reads the ramabana file. This test points ramabana to a temp folder.

os.environ['RAMABANA_CONFIG'] = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'config.toml')
test_eq(openai_key(), ('', ''))
keys_path().write_text('export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-ramabana-0000"\n'); keys_path().chmod(0o600)
test_eq(openai_key(), ('sk-ramabana-0000', str(keys_path())))
test_eq(os.getenv('OPENAI_API_KEY'), None)
set_openai_key('sk-test-1234')
test_eq(openai_key(), ('sk-test-1234', str(cfg_dir()/'keys.env')))
test_eq(oct((cfg_dir()/'keys.env').stat().st_mode & 0o777), '0o600')
test_eq(masked('sk-test-1234'), '…1234')

The engine sends the model, the hint and the WAV, with the key in the header. This test uses a fake HTTP client.

class _R:
    def raise_for_status(self): pass
    def json(self): return dict(text='hetu and sādhya')
sent = {}
def fake_post(url, **kw): sent.update(url=url, **kw); return _R()
http_post = fake_post
p = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'a.wav'; p.write_bytes(b'RIFF')
test_eq(_openai(p, 'hetu'), 'hetu and sādhya')
test_eq(sent['data'], dict(model=DFLT_OPENAI, response_format='json', prompt='hetu'))
test_eq(sent['headers']['Authorization'], 'Bearer sk-test-1234')
set_openai_key('')
keys_path().unlink()
test_fail(lambda: _openai(p), contains='no OpenAI key')
http_post = None

A key with a newline or a space can add a second line to the file. Thus set_openai_key refuses it.

test_fail(lambda: set_openai_key('sk-a\nOTHER=1'), contains='only letters')
test_fail(lambda: set_openai_key('sk a b c d e'), contains='only letters')

title: voice
text:
Transcribe
transcribe accepts a path or bytes. It writes bytes to a temporary file and removes the file after use. Without an engine, it uses current(), so a change on the Settings page applies to the next segment.


source

transcribe
def transcribe(
    audio, engine:str=None, hint:str='', model:str=None
)->str:
Text for a WAV file or WAV bytes. hint lists words that the speaker can use, such as the name of the concept.


wav_seconds gives the length of a clip in seconds. silence makes a clip of silence. The app uses this clip to warm a model.


source

silence
def silence(
    secs:float=0.5
)->bytes:
WAV bytes of silence: 16 kHz, mono, 16 bit.




source

wav_seconds
def wav_seconds(
    audio:bytes
)->float:
The length of WAV bytes, in seconds; 0 when they are not WAV.


Half a second of silence is 0.5 seconds. Bytes that are not WAV give 0.

test_eq(wav_seconds(silence()), .5)
test_eq(wav_seconds(b'nope'), 0.)

title: voice
text:
Models
KNOWN lists the models that the Settings page shows first: the two local models that we measured (see the table above), and two OpenAI models. cached tells if a model is in the Hugging Face cache. It does not use the network. The repo of the local voice (POCKET, below) has many languages, so for that repo cached looks for its English model only.


source

cache_bytes
def cache_bytes(
    model:str
)->int:
The bytes of model in the Hugging Face cache so far, with the files that are still downloading.




source

cached
def cached(
    model:str
)->bool:
True when model is in the Hugging Face cache; for the local voice, when its English model is there.


search_models looks up mlx-community speech to text models on Hugging Face, with their size. It drops text to speech, aligners and diarization models, which the mlx engine cannot use. model_size gives the size of a download: for the local voice, only its English files.


source

search_models
def search_models(
    q:str='', limit:int=15, api:NoneType=None
)->list:
mlx-community speech to text models that match q, most downloaded first, with their size.




source

model_size
def model_size(
    model:str, api:NoneType=None
)->int:
The bytes that a download of model gets from Hugging Face.




source

is_stt
def is_stt(
    model:str
)->bool:
True when the repo name looks like a speech to text model.


The filter keeps speech to text and drops the others.

test_eq([is_stt(m) for m in ('mlx-community/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-8bit', 'mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16', 'mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-bf16', 'mlx-community/silero-vad', POCKET)],
        [True, True, False, False, False])

search_models gives only the speech to text models, and model_size counts only the English files of the local voice. This test uses a fake Hugging Face API, so it does not use the network.

class _Api:
    def list_models(self, **kw): return [AttrDict(id=i, downloads=n) for i, n in (('mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16', 9), ('mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16', 8))]
    def model_info(self, m, files_metadata=True): return AttrDict(siblings=[AttrDict(rfilename=f, size=10) for f in (*POCKET_FILES, 'languages/french/model.safetensors')])
test_eq(search_models('', api=_Api()), [dict(model='mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16', downloads=8, size=40)])
test_eq(model_size(POCKET, _Api()), 30)

fetch downloads a model and notes it in the settings. The local voice gets only its English model and its default voice: it loads them, so they are in memory for the first line. remove deletes a model from the cache, but only a model that fetch downloaded. Other entries in the cache belong to other programs.


source

remove
def remove(
    model:str
):
Delete model from the Hugging Face cache. Only a model that fetch downloaded.




source

fetch
def fetch(
    model:str
):
Download model into the Hugging Face cache; note it when it was not there before.


remove refuses a model that abhyasa did not download.

test_fail(lambda: remove(DFLT_WHISPER), contains='stays')

title: voice
text:
A natural voice
The board of the screen guide says one line for each step. The browser can say it with its own voice (speechSynthesis), but that voice sounds like a machine. speak gives a natural voice. There are two engines:

pocket runs Kyutai’s Pocket TTS on this Mac, with the pocket-tts-mlx package. The download is 225 MB. It has 21 English voices, and it makes a line of 4 seconds in less than 1 second. Install it with pip install abhyasa[voice].
openai sends the line to the OpenAI speech API. It is off until you set a key. Each line passes ramabana’s guard first.

browser is the third choice of the setting voice.out. Then the page speaks, and this module makes no audio. The default is pocket. Until its model is on this Mac, the browser speaks: Speaker refuses the line with the word “browser”, and the page uses its own voice.
Licences: the pocket-tts-mlx code is MIT. The Pocket TTS weights (kyutai/pocket-tts-without-voice-cloning, by Kyutai) are CC-BY-4.0.
These are the defaults. POCKET_VOICES are the 21 English voices of Pocket TTS. caro_davy is first: the owner chose it by ear. The OpenAI voices are the voices of its speech API.
out_resolve fills in the default model and voice of an engine. Before 0.0.16 the local voices were kokoro and hf: they become pocket, and a voice that Pocket does not have becomes caro_davy. Thus an old settings file works, and nothing writes it again. out_current gives the voice of the settings, with its speed. out_where says where the voice runs.


source

out_where
def out_where(
    engine:str
)->str:




source

out_current
def out_current()->tuple:
The voice in use: (engine, model, voice, speed) from the settings.




source

out_resolve
def out_resolve(
    engine:str, model:str='', voice:str=''
)->tuple:
The engine, model and voice for a name; an empty model or voice gets the default of the engine. browser has no model.


The settings give Pocket with caro_davy. An old Kokoro or Hugging Face setting gives the same, with its old model and voice still in the file. OpenAI keeps its voice. An unknown engine is an error.

test_eq(out_current(), ('pocket', POCKET, 'caro_davy', 1.))
test_eq(out_resolve('pocket', '', 'mary'), ('pocket', POCKET, 'mary'))
for old in (dict(out='kokoro', out_model='mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16', out_voice='bm_george'), dict(out='hf', out_model='mlx-community/csm-1b', out_voice='')):
    update_settings('voice', **old)
    test_eq(out_current()[:3], ('pocket', POCKET, 'caro_davy'))
update_settings('voice', out='pocket', out_model='', out_voice='')
test_eq(out_resolve('openai', '', 'coral'), ('openai', DFLT_SPEECH, 'coral'))
test_fail(lambda: out_resolve('espeak'), contains='unknown')


The time of each word
The board lights each word when the voice says it. Pocket TTS and OpenAI give no word times. Thus by_letters shares the length of the audio among the words by their letters.


source

by_letters
def by_letters(
    text:str, secs:float
)->list:
A start time in seconds for each word of text in audio of secs seconds: each word takes a share by its letters.


Two words of 2 and 6 letters in 1 second: the first word starts at 0, the second after 3/10 of the second.

test_eq(by_letters('is hidden', 1.), [0., .3])
test_eq(by_letters('', 1.), [])



WAV
to_wav makes WAV bytes (mono, 16 bit) from the float samples of a model. clean_wav writes the header of a WAV again with its true length. OpenAI streams its WAV, so its header can give a wrong length.


source

clean_wav
def clean_wav(
    audio:bytes
)->bytes:
audio with a header that gives the true length of its samples.




source

to_wav
def to_wav(
    samples, rate:int
)->bytes:
WAV bytes (mono, 16 bit) for float samples from -1 to 1.


One second of samples at 24 kHz is one second of WAV. A header that says the data is very long becomes a header with the true length.

test_eq(wav_seconds(to_wav([0.] * 24000, 24000)), 1.)
import struct
w = to_wav([0.] * 2400, 24000)
bad = w[:4] + struct.pack('<I', 0xFFFFFFFF) + w[8:40] + struct.pack('<I', 0xFFFFFFFF) + w[44:]   # as a stream: the RIFF and data sizes are unknown
test_eq(wav_seconds(clean_wav(bad)), .1)



Pocket TTS
_pocket loads the model one time into the tts slot of resident, and keeps the state of each voice that it used. _pocket_say makes the audio of one line. normalize=True makes the voices equally loud: some, such as stuart_bell and peter_yearsley, are quiet. Pocket TTS has no speed, so the speed setting is only for OpenAI. When pocket-tts-mlx is not installed, the error says how to install it.


OpenAI
The openai engine posts the line to the OpenAI speech API and asks for WAV. instructions can set the tone (“calm, like a teacher”); only the gpt-4o models read it. The owner’s rule is that each text that goes to a hosted model passes ramabana’s guard (abhyasa.guide.guard, with ramabana.guard.outgoing). It masks a secret and refuses personal data when the privacy setting says so.


speak
speak gives the WAV bytes of one line and the start time of each of its words. Without an engine, it uses the voice of the settings. For the browser voice, it refuses: the page speaks then.


source

speak
def speak(
    text:str, engine:str=None, model:str=None, voice:str=None, speed:float=None, instructions:str=''
)->tuple:
WAV bytes for text, and the start time in seconds of each of its words (split on white space).




Tests with a fake model
A fake Pocket TTS: it gives 0.25 s of silence for each word, and it notes each voice state that it makes. The loader is a fake too, so the test downloads nothing.

import numpy as np


class _Pocket:
    sample_rate = 24000
    def __init__(self): self.said, self.voices = [], []
    def get_state_for_audio_prompt(self, v): self.voices.append(v); return dict(voice=v)
    def generate_audio(self, st, text, normalize=False):
        self.said.append((st['voice'], text, normalize))
        return np.zeros(6000 * len(text.split()), np.float32)
loads = []
_real_load, _pocket_load = _pocket_load, (lambda: loads.append(1) or (_Pocket(), {}))

speak gives one second of WAV for four words, and a time for each word that goes up. The second line does not load the model again, and a voice state loads one time.

wav, words = speak('Noise goes in, slowly.', 'pocket')
test_eq(wav_seconds(wav), 1.)
test_eq(words, by_letters('Noise goes in, slowly.', 1.))
test_eq(words, sorted(words))
speak('Again.', 'pocket', voice='mary'); speak('Once more.', 'pocket', voice='mary')
pk = _slots['tts'][0].obj[0]
test_eq((loads, pk.voices, pk.said[-1]), ([1], ['caro_davy', 'mary'], ('mary', 'Once more.', True)))

The settings choose the voice when speak has no engine. The browser voice makes no audio here.

update_settings('voice', out='pocket', out_voice='paul')
speak('hello')
test_eq(pk.said[-1][0], 'paul')
update_settings('voice', out='browser', out_voice='')
test_fail(lambda: speak('hello'), contains='browser')

The OpenAI engine refuses with no key. With a key, it sends the text after the guard, with the model, the voice and the tone. Here a fake guard puts a mark on each text, so the test sees that each text passed it.

import abhyasa.guide


real_guard, abhyasa.guide.guard = abhyasa.guide.guard, lambda s, model=None, mode=None: f'[{model.name}] {s}'
test_fail(lambda: speak('hello', 'openai'), contains='no OpenAI key')
set_openai_key('sk-test-1234')
class _W:
    content = to_wav([0.] * 12000, 24000)
    def raise_for_status(self): pass
sent = {}
http_post = lambda url, **kw: sent.update(url=url, **kw) or _W()
wav, words = speak('Look at the noise.', 'openai', instructions='calm, like a teacher')
test_eq(sent['url'], OPENAI_SPEECH_URL)
test_eq(sent['json'], dict(model=DFLT_SPEECH, voice='marin', input='[openai] Look at the noise.', response_format='wav', speed=1., instructions='[openai] calm, like a teacher'))
test_eq((wav_seconds(wav), len(words)), (.5, 4))

tts-1 does not read instructions, so the engine does not send them. Then the test puts back the real guard, the real HTTP client and the real loader.

speak('Hi.', 'openai', 'tts-1', instructions='calm')
assert 'instructions' not in sent['json']
abhyasa.guide.guard, http_post = real_guard, None
set_openai_key('')
_pocket_load = _real_load
unload('tts')



One worker for the voice
Speaker has one worker thread for all the calls of the speaking voice, separate from the speech to text worker. Thus a line of the board does not wait for a segment of dictation. It keeps the lines that it said in this run (at most most), by engine, model, voice, speed and text. The board asks for the same line again when the learner goes back a step, and that line then comes at once. Two requests for the same line share one call. warm loads the model in use with one short line, so the first line of a board does not wait for the load. The browser voice and OpenAI have nothing to load.
A model that is not on this Mac yet is not downloaded for a line: the Settings page shows its download. Until then, say refuses the line with the word “browser”, as for the browser voice, so the page and the Mac app speak with their own voice.


source

Speaker
def Speaker(
    fn:NoneType=None, most:int=64, here:NoneType=None
):
One worker thread for the speaking voice, and the lines that it said in this run.


A fake voice counts its calls. The same line comes from the cache, and a new speed is a new line.

calls = []
def fake_speak(text, engine, model, voice, speed):
    calls.append((text, engine, voice, speed)); time.sleep(.02)
    return to_wav([0.] * 2400, 24000), by_letters(text, .1)
sk = Speaker(fake_speak, most=2, here=lambda m: True)
test_fail(lambda: sk.say('hi', engine='browser'), contains='browser')
r = sk.say('Look  here.', engine='pocket')
test_eq((r['cached'], r['where'], r['voice'], r['words']), (False, 'on this Mac', 'caro_davy', by_letters('Look here.', .1)))
test_eq(sk.say('Look here.', engine='pocket')['cached'], True)
sk.say('Look here.', engine='pocket', speed=1.5)
test_eq(len(calls), 2)

Two requests at the same time for a new line make one call. The cache keeps at most most lines: the oldest goes first.

with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex: list(ex.map(lambda _: sk.say('Both at once.', engine='pocket'), range(2)))
test_eq(len(calls), 3)
test_eq(len(sk.lines), 2)
test_eq(sk.say('Look here.', engine='pocket')['cached'], False)

A failed line is not kept. warm loads the voice of the settings one time, and does nothing for the browser voice. A model that is not here is not warmed, and a line for it says that the browser speaks.

sk = Speaker(lambda *a: 1 / 0, here=lambda m: True)
test_fail(lambda: sk.say('x', engine='pocket'))
test_eq(sk.lines, {})
update_settings('voice', out='browser')
test_is(Speaker(fake_speak).warm(), None)
update_settings('voice', out='pocket')
sk = Speaker(fake_speak, here=lambda m: True); calls.clear()
sk.warm().result(); test_is(sk.warm(), None)
test_eq((sk.status, calls), ('ready', [('Ready.', 'pocket', 'caro_davy', 1.)]))
sk = Speaker(fake_speak, here=lambda m: False)
test_is(sk.warm(), None)
test_fail(lambda: sk.say('x'), contains='browser')

title: voice
text:
Segments in order
The browser sends one segment each time you stop to think. Speech has one worker thread for all the model calls. Thus only one model is in memory, and the segments run one at a time, in the order they came. A Dictation collects the segments of one answer. next gives the text in the order of the segment numbers, also when a slow request arrives late. When the browser sends a segment again (after an error), the code does not use it two times.


source

Dictation
def Dictation(
    speech, hint:str=''
):
The segments of one spoken answer: each is transcribed on the speech worker, and the text comes out in order.


Speech owns the worker. warm loads the model in use with half a second of silence, so the first segment does not wait for it. use changes the engine and model, saves the change, and warms the new model.


source

Speech
def Speech(
    fn:NoneType=None
):
One worker thread for every speech model call, and the open dictations.



Tests with a fake engine
This fake engine is slow on even segments, so the requests finish out of order. The text must still come out in order.

calls = []
def slow_fake(audio, hint=''):
    n = int(audio.decode())
    calls.append(n)
    time.sleep(.05 if n % 2 == 0 else 0)
    return f'segment {n} ({hint})'
sp = Speech(slow_fake)
d = sp.runs[sp.start('hetu')]

Segments 0 to 5 arrive out of order, from several threads. Segment 3 comes two times.

order = [2, 0, 1, 3, 3, 5, 4]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex: added = list(ex.map(lambda n: d.add(n, str(n).encode()), order))
test_eq(sum(added), 6)
d.stop(6)
out = []
while not (r := d.next(5)).get('done'): out.append(r)
test_eq([r['seq'] for r in out], list(range(6)))
test_eq(out[0]['text'], 'segment 0 (hetu)')
test_eq(sorted(calls), list(range(6)))

All the model calls ran on the one worker thread, one at a time.

seen = set()
sp.submit(lambda: seen.add(threading.current_thread().name)).result()
test_eq(len(seen), 1)
test_eq(d.pending, 0)

An engine error gives an empty text with the error. It does not stop the segments after it.

def flaky(audio, hint=''):
    if audio == b'bad': raise RuntimeError('no model')
    return 'ok'
sp = Speech(flaky)
d = sp.runs[sp.start()]
d.add(0, b'bad'); d.add(1, b'good'); d.stop(2)
test_eq(d.next(5), dict(seq=0, text='', error='no model'))
test_eq(d.next(5), dict(seq=1, text='ok'))
test_eq(d.next(5), dict(done=True))

Without stop, next waits and then gives None. use saves the choice and warms the new model with silence.

d = sp.runs[sp.start()]
test_is(d.next(.05), None)
heard = []
sp = Speech(lambda a, hint='': heard.append(wav_seconds(a)) or '')
sp.use('parakeet').result()
test_eq(current(), ('mlx', DFLT_PARAKEET))
test_eq(heard, [.5])
assert sp.status.startswith('ready'), sp.status
update_settings('stt', engine='mlx', model='')

title: voice
text:
Real models
These tests use a real clip and real models. They are slow. Run them with nbdev-test --flags slow.

clip = first(p for p in (Path('../../rishi/nbs/speech.wav'), Path('../../../rishi/nbs/speech.wav')) if p.exists())   # from the repo or a worktree
if clip:
    for e in ('mlx', 'whisper'): assert transcribe(clip, e, hint='Tennyson').strip(), e
    unload()


wav, words = speak('The forward process adds a little noise at each step.', 'pocket')
assert wav_seconds(wav) > 1 and words, words

title: detect
text:
The Learn page has one box to start something new. You paste a link, a paper, a topic, a file name or some text. As you type, one quiet line says what abhyasa will do. When two readings are both likely, the box asks one short question. Options show only when they change the result.
detect makes this reading from the text only. It makes no network call and it resolves no host name. The one lookup is a match against the titles of your vault documents, and the caller does that lookup (vault_title).
A goal can name its sources: a folder on this Mac, a GitHub repo, or a folder that is in your vault. named_sources finds them by name. The caller reads the folder names from the disk one time (folder_names), and detect only looks them up, so it still makes no network call and reads no disk.
Import the link rules of sources, so the box and a walk from a link agree on what a paper and a local address are.

title: detect
text:
The words
Each reading has one quiet line. The numbers in the lines come from the settings, so a line is never false.

title: detect
text:
Folding a name
A title matches when it is the same text with case and marks folded, so Maghā finds magha. Only case and marks fold: nakṣatras does not find Nakshatras. This is the fold of the concepts list.


source

fold
def fold(
    s
)->str:
s in lower case with no marks, and with the spaces at its ends removed.



test_eq(fold('  Maghā '), 'magha')

title: detect
text:
One source
source_of reads one word as a source: a paper, a GitHub repository, a docs site, a video, a local link or a folder. A word with no shape of a source gives None. A bare github.com/..., a name with a dot and a slash, or a host with a known ending such as example.com, gets https://. The video hosts are the video hosts of research.SOCIAL. A folder is a path that starts with / or ~, or a folder name in folders. A bare owner/name, such as fastai/diffusion-nbs, is a GitHub repository.


source

source_of
def source_of(
    s:str, folders:tuple=()
)->tuple | None:
The kind of the one word s as a source, and its link or path; None when s does not have the shape of a source.




source

as_url
def as_url(
    s:str
)->str | None:
s as a web link: as it is, with https:// for a bare link, or None.


A word with no shape of a source, such as a topic, gives None. local_name resolves no name, so printer.local is local with no lookup.

test_eq(source_of('github.com/a/b'), ('repo', 'https://github.com/a/b'))
test_eq(source_of('arxiv:1706.03762'), ('paper', '1706.03762'))
test_eq(source_of('~/code/course22')[0], 'folder')
test_eq(source_of('course22', folders=('course22',))[0], 'folder')
test_eq(source_of('http://printer.local/')[0], 'local')
test_eq(source_of('attention'), None)
test_eq(source_of('example.com'), ('site', 'https://example.com'))
test_eq(source_of('node.js'), None)
test_eq(source_of('fastai/diffusion-nbs'), ('repo', 'https://github.com/fastai/diffusion-nbs'))
test_eq(source_of('and/or'), None)

title: detect
text:
Named sources
folder_names reads the folder names under the source folders (the setting sources.roots), depth levels down. It leaves out dot folders and the build folders of SKIP_DIRS. It folds each name, so Course22 finds course22. Two folders can have the same name, so each name gives a list of paths. This is the one part that reads the disk. The app does it one time and keeps the result.


source

folder_names
def folder_names(
    roots, depth:int=2
)->dict:
Each folder name under roots, folded, to its paths: depth levels down, with no dot folder and no SKIP_DIRS folder.


A small tree: two folders named notes at two depths, a dot folder, and a folder three levels down that is too deep.

import tempfile


top = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
for d in ('course22/nbs/deep', 'other/Notes', 'notes', '.hidden/x', 'proj/node_modules'): (top/d).mkdir(parents=True)
fn = folder_names([top, top/'not-there'])
test_eq(sorted(fn), ['course22', 'nbs', 'notes', 'other', 'proj'])
test_eq(len(fn['notes']), 2)

named_sources finds the sources that a text names. It gets the folder names and the roots in the vault. It makes no network call, and it reads the disk only to find a path with spaces. Each source is a chip, with:

kind: folder, repo, gh, doc or link;
name, path, count (the documents in the vault, when it knows), and filed (it is in your vault already);
id: what the Start form sends: vault:<root>, folder:<path>, repo:<path>, gh:<owner>/<name>, doc:<doc_id> or link:<url>.

A root that is in the vault wins over a folder on the disk with the same name. A name of a common folder, such as src or data, is never a source: a goal uses these words for other things. A document title matches only as a whole phrase of at least 6 characters, with a space or a sign in it, so a one-word title does not match a plain word.


source

named_sources
def named_sources(
    text:str, titles:tuple=(), names:dict=None, roots_in_vault:tuple=()
)->list:
The sources that text names, as chips. titles: a dict of title to document id; names: from folder_names; roots_in_vault: the roots, or a dict of root to count.




source

is_path
def is_path(
    s
)->bool:


Two folders with the same name give two chips, each with its path. A common folder name gives none.

cs = named_sources('Use notes and data, and fastai/fastcore', names=fn)
test_eq([c.id for c in cs], ['folder:' + str(p) for p in fn['notes']] + ['gh:fastai/fastcore'])
test_eq(named_sources('Use fastai/fastcore', roots_in_vault={'fastai/fastcore': 9})[0], _chip('folder', 'fastai/fastcore', count=9, filed=True, id='vault:fastai/fastcore'))
test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources('Read Attention Is All You Need first', {'Attention Is All You Need': 'd1', 'Attention': 'd2'})], ['doc:d1'])

Two paths in one paste give two chips. A space, a new line or a comma can come between them. A path can have spaces in its name: put it in quotes, or paste it as it is when the folder is on the disk. Then the longest part that is on the disk is the path. This is the one check of the disk in named_sources.

a, b = top/'course22', top/'other'
for sep in (' ', '\n', ', ', ','): test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources(f'{a}{sep}{b}')], [f'folder:{a}', f'folder:{b}'])

A folder with a space in its name stays one chip, alone or before another path. A quoted path is one chip, also when it is not on the disk.

sp = top/'My notes'; sp.mkdir()
test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources(str(sp))], [f'folder:{sp}'])
test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources(f'{sp} {a}')], [f'folder:{sp}', f'folder:{a}'])
test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources(f'"{top}/Not here yet" {a}')], [f'folder:{top}/Not here yet', f'folder:{a}'])

on_disk is the disk part, for the caller: a folder chip with a .git folder is a local repo (repo:<path>), and a folder that abhyasa does not file gets why, from folder_why. It does not run git: a repo on the disk is text that abhyasa does not trust.


source

on_disk
def on_disk(
    chips
)->list:
chips, with what the disk says: a folder with .git is a repo; and a folder that abhyasa does not file has why.



test_eq(on_disk(named_sources('/tmp/no-such-folder-x'))[0].why, 'abhyasa reads only folders in your home folder.')

title: detect
text:
The reading
detect gives an AttrDict:

kind: one of empty paper repo site doc topic text ask video local folder sources goal file_name.
line: the quiet line.
ask: None, or the question, with two answers as (label, kind), and doc: the id of the vault document, when it names one.
options: the fields that matter, from pages tool title subject find.
send: the fields of /walk/new for this reading.
sources: for sources, each source as (kind, link or path).
chips: the sources that the text names (named_sources). Start files each one that is not in the vault.

A goal is one line of 7 to 60 words with “I want”, “I would like”, “help me”, “teach me”, “how do I” or “how to”, or a line that names a found source. A folder is a path. counts holds what the caller found on the disk for a path: notebooks, files, repo, or why it is refused. The folder then asks: “Walk through it” or “Use it for a goal”. names, roots_in_vault and docs (a dict of title to id) go to named_sources.
pick is the answer to a question: doc, topic or text. file is the name of a dropped file: a .pdf is in the vault as the document doc, and a .md or .txt is in the box as text.


source

detect
def detect(
    text:str, titles:tuple=(), research:bool=True, pages:int=8, file:str='', folders:tuple=(), pick:str='',
    doc:str='', names:dict=None, roots_in_vault:tuple=(), counts:dict=None, docs:dict=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
What abhyasa does with text from the Start box. titles: vault titles to match, or a dict of title to document id; folders: folder names that you named.

title: detect
text:
The cases
DETECT_CASES holds each shape that the box knows, with the kind it must give. The tests of the app use the same table.
Each case gives its kind.

for t, ti, k in DETECT_CASES: test_eq(detect(t, ti).kind, k)

A vault title asks first. Its first answer walks through the document, and the answer doc sends its title as ref.

r = detect('Nakshatras', ('Nakshatras',))
test_eq(r.ask.a, ('Walk through that document', 'doc'))
test_eq(r.ask.q, 'Nakshatras is in your vault.')
test_eq(detect('nakshatras', ('Nakshatras',), pick='doc').send, dict(ref='Nakshatras'))
test_eq(detect('Nakshatras', ('Nakshatras',), pick='topic').kind, 'topic')
test_eq(detect('nakshatras', {'Nakshatras': 'd1'}).ask.doc, 'd1')   # with a dict, the question carries the document id
test_eq(detect('nakshatras', {'Nakshatras': 'd1'}, pick='doc', doc='d1').send, dict(ref='d1'))

With research off, the topic line says that the tutor uses its own knowledge.

assert 'own knowledge' in detect('how attention works', research=False).line
test_eq(detect('how attention works').send, dict(topic='how attention works'))

Pasted text shows Title, Subject and Find concepts only. A sentence of 7 to 12 words answered as a text is one line of text.

test_eq(detect('a\nb').options, ('title', 'subject', 'find'))
test_eq(detect('a\nb').line, 'Pasted text, 2 lines. abhyasa finds the ideas in it and makes a walk.')
test_eq(detect('The moon spends about one day in each of the lunar mansions.', pick='text').kind, 'text')

A repo ticks the tool box. A site says how many pages it reads. A paper says how many ideas a walk has at most.

r = detect('github.com/vedicreader/fossick')
test_eq((r.options, r.send), (('tool',), dict(url='https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick', tool='on')))
test_eq(detect('https://docs.python.org/3/', pages=5).line, 'A docs site. abhyasa reads the pages in this folder. It reads at most 5 pages.')
test_eq(detect('1706.03762').line, 'An arXiv paper. abhyasa reads it in full and makes a walk of up to 12 ideas.')
test_eq(detect('arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762').send, dict(url='https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762'))

A file name is never a topic: it is the vault document of that name, or a hint to drop the file. A dropped file is certain: the box never asks for it.

test_eq(detect('Nakshatras', ('Nakshatras',), file='naks.pdf').line, 'A PDF. abhyasa reads it in full.')
test_eq(detect('My paper', file='My paper.pdf', doc='d7').send, dict(ref='d7'))
r = detect('Line one.\nLine two.', file='notes.md')
test_eq((r.kind, r.line, r.options, r.send['title']), ('text', 'A text file. abhyasa finds the ideas in it.', ('title', 'subject'), 'notes'))

Several sources at once give each source, and one chip for each. A folder name that you named is a folder.

r = detect('github.com/a/b, ~/code/fastbook')
test_eq(r.sources, (('repo', 'https://github.com/a/b'), ('folder', '~/code/fastbook')))
test_eq(r.send['sources'], ['gh:a/b', 'folder:' + str(Path('~/code/fastbook').expanduser())])
test_eq(detect('course22', folders=('course22',)).kind, 'folder')
r = detect('~/code/course22p2\n~/code/fastbook')
test_eq((r.line, [c.name for c in r.chips]), (LINES['sources'].format(n=2), ['course22p2', 'fastbook']))

A goal names its sources. Here the folder names come from a fake disk, and course22p2 is in the vault. The chips are a folder on the disk, a folder in the vault and a GitHub repo.

names = {'course22': [Path('~/code/personal/orgs/course22').expanduser()], 'fastbook': [Path('/h/o/fastbook')]}
r = detect(GOAL, names=names, roots_in_vault=['course22p2'])
test_eq(sorted(c.id for c in r.chips), sorted(['folder:' + str(names['course22'][0]), 'folder:/h/o/fastbook', 'gh:fastai/diffusion-nbs', 'vault:course22p2']))
assert 'reads the sources below first' in r.line
test_eq(r.send['goal'], GOAL)

With research off, the goal line says that ideas with no passage keep the tutor’s words. A goal that names no source says that abhyasa looks on the web.

assert "keep the tutor's words" in detect(GOAL, research=False).line
test_eq(detect('help me learn how attention works in a transformer').line, LINES['goal_alone'])

A folder with its count from the disk asks what to do. pick='walk' sends the folder. A refused folder says why.

p = str(Path('~/code/x').expanduser())
r = detect('~/code/x', counts={p: dict(notebooks=44, files=50)})
test_eq((r.line, r.ask.a, r.ask.b, r.ask.chip), ('A folder with 44 notebooks. abhyasa files them in your vault.', ('Walk through it', 'walk'), ('Use it for a goal', 'goal'), f'folder:{p}'))
test_eq(detect('~/code/x', counts={p: dict(notebooks=0, files=1, repo=True)}, pick='walk').send, dict(sources=[f'repo:{p}']))
test_eq(detect('/tmp/x', counts={'/tmp/x': dict(why='abhyasa reads only folders in your home folder.')}).line, 'abhyasa reads only folders in your home folder.')
test_eq(detect('course22', names=names).chips[0].path, str(names['course22'][0]))

title: detect
text:
The vault title
vault_title finds the one document on the main shelf whose title is the text, with case and marks folded, and gives its title and its id. It skips your walks, talks and concepts. A text of more than 6 words never matches. The box asks after each pause in your typing, so the folded titles are kept in an index. One small query checks if the vault changed (its count of documents, the time of the newest, and the length of all titles); only then is the index made again.


source

vault_title
def vault_title(
    vault, q:str
)->tuple | None:
The (title, id) of the document on vault (the main shelf) that is q, or q with no file ending, folded; None when there is none.




source

title_index
def title_index(
    vault
)->dict:
The folded titles of the documents on vault, each to (title, id). Made again only when the vault changed.


A test vault with one document named Nakshatras. A part of the title does not match. A new document shows at once.

from abhyasa.store import temp_learning


lr = temp_learning()
d = lr.vault.add('Some text about nakshatras.', title='Nakshatras', source='test://n')
test_eq(vault_title(lr.vault, ' NAKSHATRAS '), ('Nakshatras', d['doc_id']))
test_eq(vault_title(lr.vault, 'naksha'), None)
lr.vault.add('Some text about rasis.', title='Rasis', source='test://r')
test_eq(vault_title(lr.vault, 'rasis.pdf')[0], 'Rasis')

title: tutor
text:
This module runs the learning loop. pick chooses the concept and the depth, and a model writes the question. The learner answers and can ask for hints. The model grades the answer, and the learner model updates the concept. After a miss, the tutor teaches the smallest step. Each surface (the web app, the ramabana terminal agent, a notebook) uses Tutor and Session.
Import the tools that this module uses, and the other abhyasa modules that the tutor calls.

title: tutor
text:
Tries and hints
A wrong answer does not end the question. The tutor names the first error, gives no fix, and the learner tries again. After the tries of the setting checks.tries (3 by default), or when the learner stops, the tutor teaches the smallest step. Then the state of the concept records the miss. A pass after a wrong try counts as fragile. The best try counts: each try keeps its grade. When a try had the grade of checks.near (7 by default) or more, the close is a fragile pass, not a miss, because the learner had the idea.
Each open question keeps a thread, q.turns: the question, then each message of the learner and each reply of the tutor, in order. A message of the learner is only what they say this time, often a follow-up to the last nudge. They do not send the full answer again. The grade, the hints and the lesson read the whole thread.
HINTS is the hint ladder, from the least to the most revealing. The model gets one rung for each hint request.
DEPTH_ASK tells the model what a question at each depth must make the learner do. It is the prompt depths, one line for each depth, so you can change it on the Settings page. depth_ask reads it when a question is written.


source

depth_ask
def depth_ask(
    depth:int
)->str:
What a question at depth (1 to 5) must make the learner do, from the prompt depths.


TUTOR_SP is the system prompt for questions, hints and lessons.
The page renders markdown. So the prompt asks for maths between $...$ and for code in a fenced block with its language. Then a question with code keeps its lines.

assert 'between $...$ for maths' in TUTOR_SP
assert 'fenced code block' in TUTOR_SP and '```python' in TUTOR_SP

title: tutor
text:
Prompts
Each prompt function makes the text for one model call. The prompt text is an instruction to the model.
QUESTION_RULES is the fixed instruction for each new question. A question asks one thing, in under 60 words and in plain words. Pairs of a bad and a good question show each rule. asks_twice is a quick check on a written question: it finds a second ask after a comma, or a second question mark.


source

asks_twice
def asks_twice(
    q:str
)->bool:
True when a question has more than one ?, or a second ask joined to the first (see one_ask).




source

one_ask
def one_ask(
    q:str
)->bool:
No second ask in the sentence that ends in ‘?’. A second ask joins with ‘and’ or ‘or’ (‘, and why’). A clause before a question word (‘If x is 3, what …’) is one ask.


_concept_block describes the concept and the learner. question_prompt asks for one question at one depth. who is the profile of the learner as text (see profile), so the question uses their world.


source

with_code

    text:str, code:str='', lang:str='python'
)->str:
text after code in a fenced block, so the code keeps its lines; text alone when there is no code.

question_prompt
def question_prompt(
    c, depth, avoid:tuple=(), ctx:str='', who:str='', bridge:tuple=(), method:str='', read:str=''
):
The prompt that writes one question on c at depth in method; bridge names known ideas that a transfer question can connect to.


A transfer question asks the learner to use an idea in a new place. The best new place is one that they already know. bridges names up to three concepts that the learner knows to depth 3 or more: from other subjects first, then linked ones, then the deepest. Thus a transfer question on attention can use a Sanskrit or jyotiṣa idea.

The names of up to n concepts known to depth 3 or more, for a transfer question on c: other subjects first, then linked ones.


thread_text writes the thread as plain lines for a prompt. GRADE_SP and grade_prompt grade the conversation against the hidden model answer and the rubric. The latest message comes last, with the confidence that the learner gave it. A nudge after a wrong try is short: what is right, then one question. The way to teach does not force code into each nudge.

title: tutor
text:
Prompts that you can change
The instruction text of each prompt is in the registry of prompts, so you can change it in Settings. The constants stay as the defaults. A prompt function reads the text when it runs, so a change works on the next question. hints gives the hint ladder in use. A saved ladder must have 6 lines, and a lesson instruction must keep the ‘Check:’ line.

hints

The hint ladder in use: your 6 saved lines, else HINTS.

title: tutor
text:
Open questions on the shelf
The tutor keeps each open question in memory, and also on the shelf as a document of kind open-q. The document has the full question: the text, the concept, the kind, the options, the answer key, the tries, the hints, the confidence, the session and the walk step. Only the server reads it. A restart of the app thus loses no open question.
put_open_q writes the document under the lock of the question. A closed question stays on the shelf with its status and its end (closed, dropped or abandoned), so that an old copy, such as the open question in a session document, cannot open it again. open_q reads it.


source

Learning.put_open_q
def put_open_q(
    q, status:str='open', end:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
Save question q with its status, under its lock. A closed question never opens again: then the save does nothing and gives None.




source

Learning.open_q
def open_q(
    qid:str
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
The document of question qid as its meta, with the full question in q; None when the shelf does not have it.


stale is true for an open question with no change in checks.open_days days. The age counts from the last change, so a question that you worked on yesterday is not old.


source

stale

    m, now:float=None
)->bool:
True when the open-question document m has had no change in checks.open_days days.


Open is the open dict of the tutor. A new question goes on the shelf, and save writes each change. A question that is not in memory loads from the shelf when it is open and not stale. A stale question closes as abandoned, with no grade. del closes a question that the tutor graded, and pop closes a question that the learner left.

Open questions by id: in memory, saved on the shelf on each change, and loaded from the shelf after a restart.

title: tutor
text:
The tutor
Tutor keeps the open questions and the check questions from lessons. _ready_q finds a question that came with the source of a concept. After each observe_every closed questions, observe (from profile) reads the recent answers in the background and updates the profile.

Tutor

    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, goal:int=None, context:bool=None, sources:NoneType=None,
    pool:NoneType=None, observe_every:int=6

The learning loop over a Learning store with an ask(prompt, sp) model; pool runs background jobs.

title: tutor
text:
Ask a question
ask_on uses the first source that it finds: the check from the last lesson, a ready question, or a new question from the model. It shuffles the options of a choice question, and starts the thread with the question. public removes the fields that the learner must not see.


source

public
def public(
    q
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
A question as the learner can see it: no model answer, no rubric, no correct option, no misconception tags.




source

Tutor.ask_on
def ask_on(
    c, depth:int, why:str='', session:str='', mode:str=None, method:str=None, meta:dict=None, read:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Write a question on concept c at depth in a method from choose (or method), keep it open, and return it without its answer fields. mode='drill' uses your best method. meta goes in each attempt record; read is the text that the learner just read.


A question with code gets the code in a fenced block first, so its lines stay. A question without code stays as it is.

q = with_code('What does it return?', 'def f(x):\n    return x + 1')
assert q.startswith('```python\ndef f(x):\n    return x + 1\n```') and q.endswith('What does it return?')
assert with_code('Why?', '') == 'Why?'
assert '"code": str' in question_prompt(dict(name='n', slug='n'), 2)

A question that asks twice is written again one time, with the first try in the prompt. The test gives a paired question first, then a single one.

for q in ('What must the arrow carry, and why does the right box need it?', 'Which team matches a recurrent model, and why?', 'What moves, and what stays fixed?', 'Why? What?'): assert asks_twice(q), q
for q in ('What is X, and how is it used?', 'What is X or how is it used?'): assert asks_twice(q), q
for q in ('Why does it print 7, not 8?', 'A user, who types fast, sends two lines. Which line arrives first?', 'If the list is sorted, what does f return?',
          'When x is 3, why does f print 7?', 'In a loop with n items, how many calls happen?', 'For the input 5, where does the value go?'): assert not asks_twice(q), q   # a clause first is one ask
from abhyasa.llm import Fake
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
paired = iter([dict(question='What moves, and what stays fixed?', answer='a', rubric=['a']), dict(question='What stays fixed?', answer='a', rubric=['a'])])
lr = temp_learning(); c = lr.put('Fixed point', 'A point that stays.', 'ml')
fk = Fake(dflt=lambda p, sp: next(paired))
t = Tutor(lr, fk, sources=[]); q = t.ask_on(c, 3, method='words')
test_eq(q.question, 'What stays fixed?'); test_eq(len(fk.calls), 2)
assert 'asked twice' in fk.calls[1][0] and 'What moves, and what stays fixed?' in fk.calls[1][0]

The depth for the pace of the learner: at gentle, at most one above the floor; at fast, one more than pick gives.

The (pace, note) for the next question of a session: one pace easier after two misses, one pace harder after n solid passes.

title: tutor
tutor
text:
Grade an answer
_grade grades a choice question in code and other questions with the model.
answer adds the message of the learner to the thread, and the nudge after a wrong try. A pass or the last try closes the question.



answer
def answer(
    qid:str, answer:str='', thinking:str='', confidence:int=None, dont_know:bool=False
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Grade an answer. A wrong try keeps the question open with a nudge. A pass or the last try closes it and updates the concept.

title: tutor
text:
Stop and teach
give_up closes the question as a miss, unless an earlier try was graded checks.near or more. _close updates the concept, teaches after a miss and records the attempt. Before the lesson, a function in LESSON_HOOKS can pick another way for the lesson. The result names that way in lesson_way. Then each function in CLOSE_HOOKS can add to the result. The demo module uses this hook to attach a demo after a miss. The confidence of the first try counts, because the first try shows what the learner believed.



give_up
def give_up(
    qid:str, confidence:int=0, dont_know:bool=False
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Close the question as a miss and teach the smallest step. A shown answer is a miss, unless a try had a grade of checks.near or more.


_lesson writes the lesson after a miss. When the model fails, the lesson is a note with the model answer.


source

NoLesson
def NoLesson(
    *args, **kwargs
):
The note that stands for a lesson when the model fails; a caller can tell it from a real lesson by its type.


The tutor keeps the last 20 closed questions in shut. teach gives a lesson on one of them when you ask for it, for example after a shaky pass. It does not change the learner state. A second call gives the same lesson.


source

Tutor.teach
def teach(
    qid:str, another:bool=False
)->str:
A lesson on request for the closed question qid, kept in its thread and on its attempt. another uses a different method. The learner state does not change.

title: tutor
text:
A session
Session keeps one sitting together. Its id goes on each attempt, and it stops after limit questions (by default, the session length in the profile of the learner). It asks about one concept for at most run questions in a row. This lets the range between floor and ceiling close, and it keeps the learner interested.
A session is saved on the shelf after each move: when a question opens, after each answer and hint, and at the end. It keeps the log of each closed question (with the floor before and after, and the thread) and the open question with its thread. Thus Session.load continues it after a restart, with the same question, graded the same way.
A session in a walk asks about the current step of the walk. When the step is learned, the next question is on the next step.


source

Session
def Session(
    tutor:__main__.Tutor, focus:str=None, subject:str=None, limit:int=None, run:int=3, journey:str=None,
    sid:str=None, drill:bool=False
):
One sitting: questions and answers, saved on the shelf after each move, so that a restart can continue it.


A check right after a lesson shows that you understood it. It does not show that you will remember it, because the lesson is still in your mind. Thus each concept that you miss in a session comes back one more time before the end. At least two other questions come between the miss and the retest. retests finds these concepts. A pass right after the miss does not count.


source

retests
def retests(
    log, gap:int=None
)->dict:
The concepts missed in a session log, with no pass at least gap questions after the miss: concept -> its last miss, oldest first.


_retest asks one of them when only enough questions are left to retest each miss once.
A drill session (“Practice my weak spots”) asks your weakest concepts first, each one time, with your best method. When none is left, the session goes on as usual.
answer, give_up and hint act on the open question and save the session. A closed question goes in the log with what moved.

title: tutor
text:
Tests
A fake model plays the tutor. Its grader passes an answer only when the answer has the words “rank position”. Two concepts are on the shelf, and Reciprocal rank fusion needs Ranking.

from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
from abhyasa.llm import Fake


lr = temp_learning()
lr.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml', order=0)
lr.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Merge ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank).', 'ml', prereqs=['ranking'], order=1)
def grader(p, sp):
    ok = 'rank position' in p.split("Learner's answer:")[1]
    return dict(correct=ok, grade=8 if ok else 3, first_error='You add raw scores.',
                               misconception='scores are comparable across systems', feedback='Look at what each list really shares.')
fake = Fake({'You grade one answer': grader, 'Give hint level': 'Look at what the two lists have in common.',
             'Teach the smallest step': 'Only positions are shared. Check: what happens with k = 0?',
             'Write ONE question': dict(question='Why does RRF use ranks, not scores?', answer='Scores are not comparable.', rubric=['ranks are comparable'])})
t = Tutor(lr, fake, context=False)

The first question is on the prereq, at depth 3. The learner does not see the answer or the rubric.

q = t.next()
test_eq((q.concept, q.depth, q.kind), ('ranking', 3, 'explain'))   # rrf waits for its prereq
assert 'answer' not in q and 'rubric' not in q

A wrong answer keeps the question open and names the first error. Then a hint comes from the ladder.

r = t.answer(q.id, 'sum the scores', confidence=90)
test_eq((r.done, r.correct, r.tries_left), (False, False, 2))
test_eq(r.first_error, 'You add raw scores.')
test_eq(t.hint(q.id), 'Look at what the two lists have in common.')

A pass after a wrong try and a hint is fragile. The floor stays, and the concept is shaky at depth 3.

r = t.answer(q.id, 'use the rank position', thinking='positions are shared', confidence=90)
test_eq((r.done, r.correct, r.outcome), (True, True, 'fragile'))   # passed, but after a wrong try and a hint
c = lr.concept('ranking')
test_eq((c.floor, c.shaky, c.seen), (0, 3, 1))
test_eq(len(lr.attempts('ranking')), 2)

The thread holds each turn in order: the question, the wrong try, its nudge, the hint and the pass.

test_eq([(x['who'], x.get('kind')) for x in q.turns],
        [('tutor', 'question'), ('you', None), ('tutor', 'nudge'), ('tutor', 'hint'), ('you', None), ('tutor', 'close')])
test_eq(lr.attempts('ranking')[0].thread[1]['text'], 'sum the scores')   # the final attempt keeps the thread

A board on an open check is one hint. The grade counts it, as it counts each hint:

bl = temp_learning(); bl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
bt = Tutor(bl, fake, context=False)
bq = bt.ask_on(bl.concept('ranking'), 2)
test_eq(bt.board_hint(bq.id, 'The board circled the two ranks.'), 1)
test_eq((bt.open[bq.id].hints, bt.open[bq.id].turns[-1]['via']), (['The board circled the two ranks.'], 'board'))
for _ in range(len(HINTS) - 1): bt.board_hint(bq.id, 'Again.')
test_eq(bt.board_hint(bq.id, 'One too many.'), None)

Three wrong tries close the question, keep the misconception and teach.

q = t.next(focus='ranking')
test_eq(q.depth, 3)    # shaky at explain: ask at explain again
for _ in range(3): r = t.answer(q.id, 'sum the scores', confidence=85)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'misconception'))
assert 'Check:' in r.lesson
c = lr.concept('ranking')
test_eq((c.ceiling, c.misconceptions), (3, ['scores are comparable across systems']))

When the lesson model fails, the question still closes, the miss counts once, and the lesson says what happened.

fl = temp_learning(); fl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
def broken(p, sp=''):
    if 'Teach the smallest step' in p: raise RuntimeError('the model is down')
    return fake(p, sp)
ft = Tutor(fl, broken, context=False)
q = ft.next()
for a in ('sum the scores', 'add the scores', 'average the scores'): r = ft.answer(q.id, a, confidence=85)
test_eq((r.done, q.id in ft.open), (True, False))
assert 'could not write the lesson' in r.lesson and 'Scores are not comparable' in r.lesson
c = fl.concept('ranking')
test_eq((c.seen, c.misses), (1, 1))
test_eq(len([a for a in fl.attempts('ranking') if a.get('final')]), 1)

The check question from the lesson comes next.

q = t.next(focus='ranking')
test_eq(q.question, 'what happens with k = 0?')   # the lesson's check comes next
t.open.clear()

A ready question from a source comes before a question from the model.

lr.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit', questions=[dict(q='Join na + asti.', a='nāsti', depth=3)])
q = t.next(subject='sanskrit')
test_eq(q.question, 'Join na + asti.')

Code grades a choice question. A wrong option gives the misconception that it matches.

fake.rules['Write ONE question'] = dict(question='Which is a sandhi?', options=[dict(text='na + asti → nāsti', misconception=''),
    dict(text='na + asti → naasti', misconception='vowels just sit side by side')], correct=0, answer='', rubric=[])
t.open.clear()
lr.update('sandhi', floor=0, ceiling=2)
q = t.next(subject='sanskrit')
test_eq(q.kind, 'choice')
r = t.answer(q.id, q.options.index('na + asti → naasti'), confidence=90)
test_eq(r.first_error, 'This option assumes: vowels just sit side by side')

A session stops after limit questions and files a summary.

fake2 = Fake({k: fake.rules[k] for k in ('You grade one answer', 'Teach the smallest step')},
             dflt=dict(question='What does a rank tell you?', answer='Its position.', rubric=['position']))
s = Session(Tutor(temp_learning(), fake2, context=False), limit=2)
s.tutor.learning.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
assert s.next() is not None
s.give_up()
assert s.next() is not None
test_eq(s.answer('the rank position', confidence=80).correct, True)
test_eq(s.next(), None)
test_eq(s.summary(), '1 of 2 passed. Concepts: ranking.')
test_eq(s.tutor.learning.session(s.id).asked, 2)          # filed as it goes, not only at the end

A session on one concept stays in its subject. It asks about the neighbors of the concept first.

sl = temp_learning()
sl.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml', order=0)
sl.put('Softmax', 'Turns scores into weights that sum to 1.', 'ml', related=['attention'], order=5)
sl.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit', order=0)
ss = Session(Tutor(sl, fake2, context=False), focus='attention')
test_eq((ss.subject, ss.near), ('ml', {'softmax'}))
sl.update('attention', floor=4, seen=1, due=1e12)   # learned, and not due: the session moves on, and stays in ml
test_eq(ss.next().concept, 'softmax')

A session is saved with its open question. load continues it in a new tutor, as after a restart, and grades the same question.

pl = temp_learning(); pl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
ps = Session(Tutor(pl, fake2, context=False), limit=3)
q1 = ps.next(); ps.give_up()
q2 = ps.next(); ps.answer('a score', confidence=60)       # a wrong try: the question stays open
t2 = Tutor(pl, fake2, context=False)                      # a restart: a new tutor with nothing open
back = Session.load(t2, ps.id)
test_eq((back.q.id, back.q.question, len(back.log), back.limit), (q2.id, q2.question, 1, 3))
assert 'answer' not in back.q and back.q.id in t2.open    # the learner view, and the full question in the tutor
test_eq(back.answer('the rank position', confidence=80).correct, True)
test_eq([(r['outcome'], r['floor0']) for r in back.log], [('gap', 0), ('fragile', 0)])
test_eq([t['who'] for t in back.log[-1]['turns']], ['tutor', 'you', 'tutor', 'you', 'tutor'])

moved gives the floor before and after for each concept of the log.

test_eq([(m['concept'], m['before'], m['after'], m['asked'], m['passed']) for m in moved(back.log)], [('ranking', 0, 0, 2, 1)])
test_eq(moved([dict(concept='a', name='A', floor0=2, floor=3, correct=True), dict(concept='a', floor0=3, floor=4, correct=True, misconception='x')]),
        [dict(concept='a', name='A', before=2, after=4, asked=2, passed=2, misconceptions=['x'])])

end closes the session. An ended session loads with no open question and gives no more questions.

back.next(); back.end()
again = Session.load(Tutor(pl, fake2, context=False), ps.id)
test_eq((again.q, again.next(), bool(again.ended)), (None, None, True))
test_is(Session.load(t2, 'nope'), None)

A session in a walk asks about the current step. When the step is learned, it goes to the next step. It stops at the end of the walk.

jl = temp_learning()
for n in ('Tokenizers', 'Embeddings', 'Sandhi'): jl.put(n, f'{n} statement.', 'ml' if n != 'Sandhi' else 'sanskrit')
jl.update('sandhi', seen=1, due=1.)                     # a review due elsewhere does not break in
j = jl.put_journey(dict(id='llms', title='LLMs', goal='LLMs', steps=[dict(slug='tokenizers', status='todo'), dict(slug='embeddings', status='todo')]))
js = Session(Tutor(jl, fake2, context=False), journey='llms')
q = js.next()
test_eq((q.concept, q.why.split(';')[0]), ('tokenizers', 'the next step of your walk "LLMs"'))   # a method note can follow
js.give_up(); jl.update('tokenizers', floor=4)
test_eq(js.next().concept, 'embeddings')
js.give_up(); jl.update('embeddings', floor=4)
test_eq((js.next(), jl.session(js.id).journey), (None, 'llms'))

The profile goes into the question prompt. At the gentle pace a new concept starts at depth 1, not 3.

gl2 = temp_learning(); gl2.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
gl2.set_profile(background='codes in Python', pace='gentle')
fk = Fake(dflt=dict(question='Which keeps its scale?', options=[dict(text='a rank', misconception=''), dict(text='a score', misconception='x')], correct=0, answer='', rubric=[]))
q = Tutor(gl2, fk, context=False).next()
test_eq(q.depth, 1)
assert 'codes in Python' in fk.calls[-1][0] and 'who' not in q

flow moves the pace by one step, and only from the last outcomes. A note comes only when the pace changes.

sol, gap = dict(outcome='solid'), dict(outcome='gap')
test_eq(flow([]), ('steady', ''))
test_eq(flow([sol, gap, dict(outcome='misconception')]), ('gentle', 'easier: you missed the last two'))
test_eq(flow([sol] * 3, 'gentle'), ('steady', 'harder: 3 clean passes in a row'))
test_eq(flow([gap, gap], 'gentle'), ('gentle', ''))     # already gentle: no change, no note
test_eq(flow([sol, sol, gap]), ('steady', ''))           # one miss is not a trend

In a session, two misses make the next question easier, and its “why” line says so. Tutor.next takes the pace from the session over the pace in the profile.

fw = temp_learning(); fw.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
fs = Session(Tutor(fw, fake2, context=False), limit=5)
for _ in range(2): fs.next(); fs.give_up()
test_eq(fs.next().why.endswith('; easier: you missed the last two'), True)
fw.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit')
test_eq(Tutor(fw, fake2, context=False).next(subject='sanskrit', pace='gentle').depth, 1)   # a new concept, at depth 1 and not 3

retests keeps a miss until a pass comes at least checks.retest questions later (2 by default). A new miss moves the concept to the end.

def lg(*xs): return [dict(concept=k, outcome=o, correct=o not in MISSES) for k, o in xs]
test_eq(retests(lg(('a', 'gap'), ('a', 'solid'))), {'a': 0})                          # a pass right after: still to retest
test_eq(retests(lg(('a', 'gap'), ('b', 'solid'), ('b', 'solid'), ('a', 'fragile'))), {})   # a later pass clears it
test_eq(retests(lg(('a', 'gap'), ('b', 'misconception'), ('a', 'gap'))), {'b': 1, 'a': 2})

When the questions left are only enough for the retests, the session asks the missed concept again, and says why. With more questions left, it does not.

rl = temp_learning(); rl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml', order=0); rl.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit', order=1)
rs = Session(Tutor(rl, fake2, context=False), limit=4)
rs.log = lg(('ranking', 'gap'), ('sandhi', 'solid'), ('sandhi', 'solid'))
q = rs.next()
test_eq((q.concept, q.why), ('ranking', 'a retest: you missed this earlier in this session'))
rs.tutor.open.clear(); rs.limit = 10
assert not rs.next().why.startswith('a retest')

bridges takes known concepts only, from other subjects first. A transfer question gets them in its prompt; an explain question does not.

bl = temp_learning()
bl.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml', related=['softmax'])
for n, s, f in (('Softmax', 'ml', 3), ('Ranking', 'ml', 4), ('Sandhi', 'sanskrit', 3), ('Nakshatra', 'jyotisha', 1)): bl.put(n, f'{n}.', s); bl.update(n.lower(), floor=f)
test_eq(bridges(bl.concept('attention'), bl.concepts()), ['Sandhi', 'Softmax', 'Ranking'])
fb = Fake(dflt=dict(question='Where else?', answer='', rubric=[]))
tb = Tutor(bl, fb, context=False)
tb.ask_on(bl.concept('attention'), 5); assert 'Sandhi' in fb.calls[-1][0]
tb.ask_on(bl.concept('attention'), 3); assert 'Sandhi' not in fb.calls[-1][0]

After each observe_every closed questions, the profile learns in the background.

class Now:
    "A pool that runs a job at once, for the test."
    def submit(self, f, *a): f(*a)
ol = temp_learning(); ol.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
fo = Fake({**fake2.rules, 'You keep a short profile': dict(changes=[dict(field='confuses', add='ranks against scores', why='You missed it twice.')])}, dflt=fake2.dflt)
ot = Tutor(ol, fo, context=False, pool=Now(), observe_every=2)
for _ in range(2): ot.give_up(ot.next().id)
test_eq(ol.profile().confuses, ['ranks against scores'])

The sources of the learner ground the question, the grade and the lesson. First, import passage, which makes one passage of a source.

from abhyasa.ground import passage

A source of notes grounds the question. The learner sees the citations only when the question closes.

class Notes:
    name = 'notes'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L([passage('vault:notes', 'n1', 'My ranking notes', 'Ranking orders items; RRF adds 1/(k + rank).')])
gl = temp_learning(); gl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
gt = Tutor(gl, fake2, sources=[Notes()])
q = gt.next()
assert 'My ranking notes' in fake2.calls[-1][0]                 # the question prompt has the passage
assert 'grounds' not in q and 'ctx' not in q                  # the learner does not see it yet
r = gt.answer(q.id, 'the rank position', confidence=80)
test_eq(r.grounds, [dict(src='vault:notes', ref='n1', title='My ranking notes', url='')])
assert 'My ranking notes' in fake2.calls[-1][0]                 # the grade prompt has it too

A function in CLOSE_HOOKS sees each closed question and can add to the result. The result names its concept.

seen = []
def spy(t, q, r): seen.append(q.concept); r.extra = 1
CLOSE_HOOKS.append(spy)
try: r = gt.answer(gt.next().id, 'the rank position', confidence=80)
finally: CLOSE_HOOKS.remove(spy)
test_eq((seen, r.extra, r.concept), (['ranking'], 1, 'ranking'))

A function in LESSON_HOOKS picks the way of the lesson after a miss. The lesson prompt uses that way, and the attempt keeps it in teach_method. The miss still counts for the way of the question.

def by_analogy(t, q): return 'analogy'
LESSON_HOOKS.append(by_analogy)
try: q = gt.ask_on(gl.concept('ranking'), 2); r = gt.give_up(q.id)
finally: LESSON_HOOKS.remove(by_analogy)
a = gl.attempts(limit=1)[0]
assert way('analogy') in fake2.calls[-1][0]
test_eq((r.lesson_way, a.teach_method, a.method), ('analogy', 'analogy', q.method))

With no hook, the lesson uses the way of the question, and lesson_way is empty.

q = gt.ask_on(gl.concept('ranking'), 2); r = gt.give_up(q.id)
test_eq((r.lesson_way, 'teach_method' in gl.attempts(limit=1)[0]), ('', False))

A follow-up is only what the learner says this time. The grade prompt has the earlier turns in order, then the follow-up. A pass on the third message, after two nudges, is fragile.

tl = temp_learning(); tl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
tt = Tutor(tl, fake, context=False)
q = tt.next()
tt.answer(q.id, 'sum the scores', confidence=60)
tt.answer(q.id, 'scale them first', confidence=60)
r = tt.answer(q.id, 'use the rank position', confidence=70)
p = next(c[0] for c in reversed(fake.calls) if 'You grade' in c[1])
assert p.index('Tutor (question)') < p.index('Learner: sum the scores') < p.index('Tutor (nudge)') < p.index('Learner: scale them first')
test_eq(p.split("Learner's answer: ")[1].split('\n')[0], 'use the rank position')   # only the follow-up
assert 'scale them first' not in p.split("Learner's answer")[1]
test_eq((r.done, r.correct, r.outcome), (True, True, 'fragile'))

title: tutor
text:
Teach on request
After a shaky pass, a lesson comes only when you ask. It leaves the learner state as the close left it, and a second ask gives the same lesson.

sl = temp_learning(); sl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
ss = Session(Tutor(sl, fake, context=False), limit=3)
q = ss.next()
for a in ('sum the scores', 'scale them first', 'use the rank position'): r = ss.answer(a, confidence=70)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'fragile'))
before = dict(sl.concept('ranking'))

The lesson builds on the first error, and the concept does not change.

lesson = ss.teach(q.id)
assert 'Check:' in lesson and 'could not' not in lesson
test_eq({k: v for k, v in sl.concept('ranking').items()}, before)
test_eq(ss.teach(q.id), lesson)
test_eq(len([x for x in ss.tutor.shut[q.id].turns if x.get('kind') == 'lesson']), 1)

The session log keeps the lesson, so a restart shows it.

test_eq(sl.session(ss.id).log[-1]['turns'][-1], dict(who='tutor', kind='lesson', text=lesson, method=ss.tutor.shut[q.id].method))

The grading prompt tells the model to explain a term that you say you do not know, and to read past speech-to-text noise.

assert "I don't know what the loop means" in GRADE_SP and 'speech to text' in GRADE_SP

A right equation meets a rubric point, even when the words of the method are missing. A right answer gets a grade of 7 or more. The grading prompt says so. It also asks for the voice of a kind teacher, not a report: “The key does not have to be a short form of the value”, not “You assume that the key must be a condensed version of the value”.

for s in ('contains or implies it', 'need not say each step in words', 'only the method or framing', '7-10', 'When `correct` is false, `grade` is 6 or less.', 'A right result from wrong reasoning is not correct.'):
    assert s in GRADE_SP, s
assert 'not like a report' in GRADE_SP and 'BAD: "You assume' in GRADE_SP and 'kind, clear person' in TUTOR_SP   # the voice of a person, not a report

The question prompt asks for rubric points that are ideas. A point is never a required word or a step of a named method.

assert 'Never make a rubric point a required word' in question_prompt(lr.concept('ranking'), 3)

title: tutor
text:
Short questions and short nudges
A question asks one thing, and a nudge after a wrong try is short. QUESTION_RULES gives the rules for a question, with pairs of a bad and a good question. The pairs use other subjects, so that they do not leak into a real question.

p = question_prompt(lr.concept('ranking'), 2, method='code')
assert QUESTION_RULES in p
for s in ('one question mark', '"Then" or "Also"', 'under 60 words', 'one question word', '"and why"', 'ASD-STE100', '`question`, `options` and `answer`'): assert s in p, s

Each rule has one pair: a BAD question and a GOOD question. There are at least four pairs, and no pair is about the neuron.

test_eq(QUESTION_RULES.count('BAD:'), QUESTION_RULES.count('GOOD:'))
assert QUESTION_RULES.count('GOOD:') >= 4 and 'neuron' not in QUESTION_RULES.lower()

A nudge says in a few words what is right, then asks one question. It shows at most 4 lines of code, and never code that the thread already shows.

for s in ('ONE question', 'at most 4 lines', 'Never repeat code', 'does not force code'): assert s in GRADE_SP, s

The way to teach still goes into the grade prompt. With the code way, the prompt asks for code in feedback only when it helps the next step.

gq = AttrDict(name='Ranking', depth=2, question='Why ranks?', answer='', rubric=['ranks'], turns=[], method='code')
gp = grade_prompt(gq, 'because')
assert METHODS['code'] in gp and 'only when it helps the next step' in gp
assert 'Write `feedback` in this way.' not in gp

with_code still puts the code of a question first, in its own fenced block.

test_eq(with_code('What does s hold before the return line?', 's = 0\nreturn s'), '```python\ns = 0\nreturn s\n```\n\nWhat does s hold before the return line?')

title: tutor
text:
Best try counts
A try with a grade of checks.near or more shows that the learner has the idea. If the question later closes as a miss, it closes as fragile instead. The lesson still shows when the tutor teaches. The concept keeps its floor and its ceiling. A model that grades each try with a set grade plays the tutor here.

test_eq(val('checks.near'), 7)
def model(*gs):
    "A fake model whose grader gives the grades `gs` in turn, all as not correct."
    it = iter(gs)
    bad = lambda p, sp: dict(correct=False, grade=next(it), first_error='You do not name the method.', misconception='', feedback='Say it in words.')
    return Fake({**fake.rules, 'You grade one answer': bad})
def miss_after(*gs, give_up=True):
    "Try once for each grade in `gs`, then ask for the lesson. The result and the concept, with a floor of 2 before."
    l = temp_learning(); l.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml'); l.update('ranking', floor=2)
    bt = Tutor(l, model(*gs), context=False); q = bt.next()
    for g in gs[:2 if give_up else 3]: r = bt.answer(q.id, 'a try', confidence=40)
    return (bt.give_up(q.id) if give_up else r), l.concept('ranking'), q

Each try keeps its grade. A try graded 8 is the best try, so the lesson still shows, but the outcome is fragile and the floor and the ceiling stay.

r, c, q = miss_after(8)
test_eq([x['grade'] for x in q.tries], [8])
test_eq((r.done, r.correct, r.outcome), (True, True, 'fragile'))
assert 'Check:' in r.lesson
test_eq((r.feedback, r.first_error, r.misconception), ('', '', ''))   # no wrong-reply nudge under the pass
test_eq((c.floor, c.ceiling, c.misses), (2, 6, 0))

A best try of 3 is no near pass. The question still closes as a gap, and the ceiling falls.

r, c, q = miss_after(3)
test_eq((r.correct, r.outcome), (False, 'gap'))
test_eq((c.floor, c.ceiling, c.misses), (2, 4, 1))

The third wrong try counts the same way. A grade of 8 in an earlier try saves it. Grades of 3, 3 and 3 do not.

r, c, q = miss_after(3, 8, 3, give_up=False)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'fragile'))
test_eq([x['grade'] for x in q.tries], [3, 8, 3])
test_eq((r.feedback, r.first_error), ('', ''))   # the third reply was wrong: its nudge does not show
r, c, q = miss_after(3, 3, 3, give_up=False)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'gap'))

A try with no grade is no near pass.

r, c, q = miss_after(None)
test_eq((r.correct, r.outcome), (False, 'gap'))

title: tutor
section: Ways to learn, and gaps you name
text:
Ways to learn, and gaps you name
Each question gets a method. The prompt says it, and the outcome counts for it when the question closes.

import random


wl = temp_learning(); wl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
seen = []
def wgrade(p, sp):
    seen.append(p); said = p.split("Learner's answer:")[1].split("Learner's think-aloud:")[0]
    if 'the loop' in said: return dict(correct=False, grade=2, first_error='You skip the sum.', misconception='', feedback='A loop adds each product.',
                                    gaps=['weighted sum as a loop'], asks_for='code')
    return dict(correct='rank position' in said, grade=8, first_error='', misconception='', feedback='Yes.', gaps=[], asks_for='')
wfake = Fake({'You grade one answer': wgrade, 'The idea: weighted sum as a loop': dict(name='Weighted sum as a loop', statement='A loop adds each weight times its input.'),
              'Teach the smallest step': 'Positions are shared. Check: what if k = 0?',
              'Write ONE question': lambda p, sp: seen.append(p) or dict(question='Why do ranks merge well?', answer='They are comparable.', rubric=['comparable'])})
wt = Tutor(wl, wfake, context=False); wt.rng = random.Random(1)
q = wt.next()
assert q.method in METHODS and f"The way to teach this time: {METHODS[q.method]}" in seen[-1]

“I don’t know what the loop means” keeps the idea as a gap of the concept, and “show me with code” switches the method for the next nudge.

r = wt.answer(q.id, "I don't know what the loop means, show me with code")
test_eq(wl.concept('ranking').gaps, ['weighted-sum-as-a-loop'])
