One top folder gives at most TREE_TOP files until each other top folder has its files; then the room that is left takes the rest, in the same order. want: paths in root to file first. cut says why it stopped early, or is ’’.




source

tree_rank
def tree_rank(
    rel, course:bool=False, want:tuple=()
)->int | None:
The place of the file at the path rel (in its folder) in the filing order, from 0, or None when abhyasa does not file it: the files that you name (want), the top README, the notebooks, the READMEs of examples/, its training scripts, its other scripts, the English docs, the other text, the other code (none in a course), and last the docs in other languages.




source

tree_ok
def tree_ok(
    p, root, most:int=None
)->bool:
Whether abhyasa may read the file p under the folder root: not a link, not a hard link, at most most bytes (default TREE_MB MB), and inside root after each link is resolved.


A small folder: two notebooks, a note, a data folder, a .git folder, a file of another type, and a link to a file outside the folder.

import tempfile
from collections import Counter
from fastcore.nbio import new_nb, mk_cell, write_nb


def two_notebooks(d):
    "Write `01_a.ipynb` and `02_b.ipynb` in the folder `d`."
    write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# Noise\n\nA diffusion model adds noise, then learns to remove it.', 'markdown'), mk_cell('x = 1')]), Path(d)/'01_a.ipynb')
    write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# Steps\n\nThe sampler removes the noise in small steps.', 'markdown')]), Path(d)/'02_b.ipynb')

top = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
d = top/'course'; (d/'data').mkdir(parents=True); (d/'.git').mkdir()
two_notebooks(d)
(d/'notes.md').write_text('# Notes\n\nThe UNet predicts the noise.')
(d/'data/big.txt').write_text('data'); (d/'.git/config.txt').write_text('git'); (d/'model.pkl').write_text('bytes')
(top/'secret.txt').write_text('outside'); (d/'link.txt').symlink_to(top/'secret.txt'); os.link(top/'secret.txt', d/'key.txt')
(d/'tool.py').write_text('print(1)')

tree_files keeps the two notebooks and the note. It skips the data folder, the .git folder, the .pkl file, the link, the hard link key.txt and, since the folder has notebooks, tool.py.

test_eq([p.name for p in tree_files(d)], ['01_a.ipynb', '02_b.ipynb', 'notes.md'])
test_eq(tree_files(d).cut, '')

The caps: with a cap of 2 files, or of 1 MB in all, tree_files keeps the first files and says why it stopped. A file over TREE_MB is never read.

was = TREE_FILES, TREE_MB, TREE_TOTAL_MB
TREE_FILES = 2
t = tree_files(d); test_eq((len(t), t.cut), (2, 'abhyasa stopped at 2 files.'))
TREE_FILES, TREE_TOTAL_MB = 400, 1
(d/'big.md').write_bytes(b'x' * (2**20 - 10))
t = tree_files(d); test_eq((t.cut, 'big.md' in [p.name for p in t]), ('abhyasa stopped at 1 MB.', False))
TREE_TOTAL_MB, TREE_MB = 200, 0.5
test_eq(('big.md' in [p.name for p in tree_files(d)], tree_files(d).cut), (False, ''))
TREE_FILES, TREE_MB, TREE_TOTAL_MB = was; (d/'big.md').unlink()

A temp tree with the shape of diffusers: a README, 30 examples with a README and a training script each, 450 English docs, 50 Korean docs, 3 notebooks and 2,000 other .py files.

big = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()/'diffusers'
def put(rel, s='x'): (big/rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (big/rel).write_text(s)
put('README.md', '# Diffusers')
for k in ['text_to_image', 'dreambooth', *[f'ex{i:02d}' for i in range(28)]]: put(f'examples/{k}/README.md'); put(f'examples/{k}/train_{k}.py')
put('examples/text_to_image/train_text_to_image_lora.py')
for i in range(450): put(f'docs/source/en/page{i:03d}.md')
for i in range(50): put(f'docs/source/ko/page{i:03d}.md')
for i in range(3): write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell(f'# Notebook {i}', 'markdown')]), big/f'nb{i}.ipynb')
for i in range(2000): put(f'src/diffusers/m{i:04d}.py')

abhyasa files 400 files. The README, the notebooks, each README and training script of examples/ are in. docs/ gives no more than its cap and the room that is left, and no Korean page. src/ gives the rest of the room.

t = tree_files(big)
rel = [p.relative_to(big).as_posix() for p in t]
test_eq((len(t), t.cut), (TREE_FILES, f'abhyasa stopped at {TREE_FILES} files.'))
for x in ['README.md', 'nb0.ipynb', 'nb2.ipynb', 'examples/text_to_image/README.md', 'examples/dreambooth/README.md',
          'examples/text_to_image/train_text_to_image_lora.py', 'examples/ex27/train_ex27.py']: assert x in rel, x
by = Counter(r.split('/')[0] if '/' in r else '' for r in rel)
test_eq((by['examples'], by['src']), (61, TREE_TOP))
assert TREE_TOP <= by['docs'] < 450 and not any('/ko/' in r for r in rel)

A file that you name comes first. A course keeps its notebooks and no other code, and a small code folder keeps all of its files.

assert 'src/diffusers/m1999.py' in [p.relative_to(big).as_posix() for p in tree_files(big, want=['src/diffusers/m1999.py'])]
test_eq((tree_rank('tool.py', course=True), tree_rank('examples/a/train_a.py', course=True), tree_rank('docs/source/en/x.md')), (None, 4, 6))
test_eq(tree_rank('docs/source/pt-BR/x.md'), 9)



Which folders abhyasa files
folder_why says why abhyasa does not file a folder, or gives ''. The folder must be a real folder in your home folder. It must not be the home folder itself, a hidden folder (a name that starts with a dot) or a link. The test folder is not in the home folder, so it is refused.


source

folder_why
def folder_why(
    p
)->str:
Why abhyasa does not file the folder p (the rules of settings.source_root_why), or ’’ when it can. It must be a folder that you can read.



test_eq(folder_why(d), 'abhyasa reads only folders in your home folder.')
test_eq(folder_why('~'), 'Name a folder in your home folder, not the home folder itself.')
test_eq(folder_why('~/.ssh'), 'abhyasa does not read a hidden folder or a link.')
test_eq(folder_why('~/no-such-folder-for-abhyasa'), NO_FOLDER)



Filing a folder
_file_tree files the files of a folder on a shelf. A notebook or a file with the same mtime as its copy on the shelf is not read again. Each document gets meta.root, meta.path and meta.mtime, and meta.url when url gives one. The result has the shape of file_link, with mtime. Its added holds only the documents that were not on the shelf before, so an Undo never forgets a document that you had before.
file_folder checks the folder with folder_why first. It raises LinkError with the plain reason. A document that was on the shelf before, filed by another tool or by an older abhyasa, keeps its meta. cut says when a cap stopped the filing.


source

file_folder
def file_folder(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, path, shelf:str='notebooks', want:tuple=()
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
File the folder path in your home folder on shelf. Each doc keeps meta.root (the folder name) and meta.path. Raises LinkError for a folder that abhyasa does not file.


The test folder files three documents with meta.root. A second filing reads nothing again and adds nothing.

lr = temp_learning()
docs = _file_tree(lr, d, 'notebooks', 'course')
test_eq(len(docs), 3)
test_eq({lr.vault.shelf('notebooks').doc(x.doc_id)['meta']['root'] for x in docs}, {'course'})
test_eq(len(docs.added), 3)
again = _file_tree(lr, d, 'notebooks', 'course')
test_eq((again, len(again.added)), (docs, 0))
test_fail(lambda: file_folder(lr, d), contains='home folder')



The roots in the vault
vault_roots gives each folder or repo on a shelf, with its count of documents. The Start box uses it to say “fastbook · 20 notebooks · in your vault”. root_docs gives the documents of one root, in path order.


source

root_docs
def root_docs(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, root:str, shelf:str='notebooks'
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
The documents of the folder or repo root on shelf, in path order, in the shape of file_link.




source

vault_roots
def vault_roots(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, shelf:str='notebooks'
)->dict:
Each folder or repo filed on shelf (its meta.root), to its count of documents.



test_eq(vault_roots(lr), {'course': 3})
test_eq(root_docs(lr, 'course').attrgot('title'), ['course/01_a', 'course/02_b', 'course/notes'])

A notebook on the notebooks shelf now opens by its title, with no shelf given.

test_eq(doc_pages(lr, 'course/02_b').title, 'course/02_b')



Undo
unfile forgets the documents of one filing. It forgets a document only when it is still the same file: the same id and the same mtime. It gives the count.


source

unfile
def unfile(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, docs
)->int:
Forget the docs that one filing added, when each is still the same file (same id, same mtime). Returns the count.



test_eq(unfile(lr, docs.added[:1]), 1)
test_eq(vault_roots(lr), {'course': 2})
test_eq(unfile(lr, docs.added[:1]), 0)   # it is gone already



A GitHub repo
gh_name reads owner/name from a GitHub link, or from the bare owner/name. A pair of common words, such as and/or, is not a repo. A host that is not github.com gives None.


source

gh_name
def gh_name(
    s:str
)->str | None:
owner/name of the GitHub repo that s names (a github.com link, or owner/name), or None.



test_eq(gh_name('fastai/diffusion-nbs'), 'fastai/diffusion-nbs')
test_eq(gh_name('https://github.com/fastai/diffusion-nbs.git'), 'fastai/diffusion-nbs')
test_eq(gh_name('github.com/fastai/course22/blob/master/README.md'), 'fastai/course22')
for s in ('and/or', '10/30', 'a/..', 'https://gitlab.com/a/b', '~/code/x', 'docs.python.org/3'): test_eq(gh_name(s), None)

file_repo clones only a public repo on github.com. It asks GitHub first (gh_public): a private repo, a repo that is not there, or a repo bigger than REPO_MB MB is refused. Then clone_repo gives the HTTPS link that was checked to fossick’s gh_clone, which clones it into fossick’s cache folder. It uses HTTPS only, never SSH, clones only the last commit (depth 1), puts -- before the link, and stops git after 600 seconds. It removes a clone that stopped half way, and it changes no environment variable. abhyasa has no clone code of its own. fossick is a core dependency, so no extra is necessary. A repo that is in the cache already is brought up to date, not cloned again. The research agent uses clone_repo too, so a repo is on the disk one time. Each document keeps meta.root='owner/name' and meta.url, the GitHub page of the file.


source

file_repo
def file_repo(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, url:str, shelf:str='notebooks', want:tuple=()
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Clone the public GitHub repo url (a link or owner/name) with clone_repo, then file it on shelf. Raises LinkError with a plain reason.




source

clone_repo
def clone_repo(
    url:str, timeout:float=600
)->tuple:
(owner/name, folder) for the public GitHub repo url (a link or owner/name), cloned or brought up to date by fossick’s gh_clone in its cache. Raises LinkError with a plain reason.




source

gh_public
def gh_public(
    owner:str, name:str
)->dict | None:
What GitHub says of the repo owner/name (private, size in KB), or None when it has no such repo. With gheasy installed, its gh_token gives a token, for more calls an hour.


gh_public sends a token from gheasy’s gh_token when gheasy is installed. GitHub gives 60 calls an hour with no token. A bad token (401) gets one more call with no token, and with no gheasy no token goes. A fake http_get stands for GitHub.

import fossick, sys, types


sent = []
def fake_get(url, **kw):
    "GitHub: 401 for a bad token, else a public repo of 10 KB."
    sent.append((kw.get('headers') or {}).get('Authorization'))
    return AttrDict(status=401 if sent[-1] == 'Bearer bad' else 200, body=b'{"private": false, "size": 10}')
was_get, mods = fossick.http_get, {k: sys.modules.get(k) for k in ('gheasy', 'gheasy.core')}
def token(t): sys.modules['gheasy'] = sys.modules['gheasy.core'] = types.SimpleNamespace(gh_token=lambda: t)
fossick.http_get = fake_get
try:
    token('good'); test_eq(gh_public('a', 'b')['size'], 10); test_eq(sent, ['Bearer good'])
    sent.clear(); token('bad'); test_eq(gh_public('a', 'b')['size'], 10); test_eq(sent, ['Bearer bad', None])   # a bad token: one more call with none
    sent.clear(); sys.modules['gheasy'] = sys.modules['gheasy.core'] = None; gh_public('a', 'b'); test_eq(sent, [None])   # no gheasy: no token
finally:
    fossick.http_get = was_get
    for k, v in mods.items():
        if v is None: sys.modules.pop(k, None)
        else: sys.modules[k] = v

A test clone: a fake fossick gh_clone copies the test folder, and a fake gh_public says that the repo is public. Nothing goes to the network.

import sys, types


cache = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
def fake_clone(url, timeout=None):
    "A clone with no network: it copies the test folder the first time, and keeps the link and the time limit that it got."
    got.append((url, timeout)); to = cache/url.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
    if not to.exists(): shutil.copytree(d, to)
    return to

got, real, real_clone = [], gh_public, fossick.gh_clone
fossick.gh_clone, gh_public = fake_clone, lambda o, n: dict(private=False, size=10)
try:
    lr = temp_learning()
    docs = file_repo(lr, 'https://github.com/fastai/course')
    m = lr.vault.shelf('notebooks').doc(docs[0].doc_id)['meta']
    test_eq((m['root'], m['url'], got), ('fastai/course', 'https://github.com/fastai/course/blob/HEAD/01_a.ipynb', [('https://github.com/fastai/course', 600)]))
    test_eq(file_repo(lr, 'fastai/course').attrgot('doc_id'), docs.attrgot('doc_id'))   # in the cache: the same documents
    gh_public = lambda o, n: dict(private=True); got.clear()
    test_fail(lambda: file_repo(lr, 'fastai/other'), contains='not a public repo'); test_eq(got, [])   # a private repo is never cloned
    gh_public = lambda o, n: dict(private=False, size=REPO_MB * 1024 + 1)
    test_fail(lambda: file_repo(lr, 'fastai/big'), contains='too big'); test_eq(got, [])
    test_fail(lambda: file_repo(lr, 'and/or'), contains='only a public repo')
finally: gh_public, fossick.gh_clone = real, real_clone

title: sources
text:
The source of a passage
The source line uses datetime for the day that the tutor read a web page.
source_of gives the source line of a passage: one label, the title, a link to the document, the place and the date. A passage from the web has the label from the web. A passage from a document of yours has your source. Text with no passage is the tutor’s own words. The walk, the talk and the recap file all draw this one line.


source

source_of
def source_of(
    read:dict, j:dict | None=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
The source line of the passage read (a step read, a slide source or a cite) in walk j: its label, its title, href (its document in the vault), place (the section and the page, or the site of a web page), url (a web page) and date. The place starts with what, the kind of text, when the passage has one (such as Summary), so a summary never reads as a quote.


A passage of a paper in the vault names the paper, the section number and the page, and links to the document.

p = source_of(dict(shelf='store', doc_id='d1', title='Attention Is All You Need', section='3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention', page=4, text='We suspect.'))
test_eq((p.label, p.title, p.href, p.place, p.url, p.date), ('your source', 'Attention Is All You Need', '/v/store/d1', 'section 3.2.1 · p. 4', '', ''))

A passage from the web names its site and the day it was read, and keeps the link to the page.

w = source_of(dict(src='web', shelf='store', doc_id='d2', title='Softmax explained', site='example.org', url='https://example.org/s', text='Q.', at=datetime(2026, 10, 29, 12).timestamp()))
test_eq((w.label, w.href, w.place, w.url, w.date), ('from the web', '/v/store/d2', 'example.org', 'https://example.org/s', '29 Oct 2026'))

A cite on a vault shelf links to its document. A step with no passage is the tutor’s words. A link that is not a web page is not kept.

test_eq(source_of(dict(src='vault:notes', ref='n1#2', title='My notes')).href, '/v/notes/n1')
test_eq(source_of(dict(src='vedicreader', ref='a:1', title='Ashtadhyayi 1 2')).place, 'vedicreader')
test_eq(source_of(dict(text=''), dict(source=dict(title='A paper'))).label, 'tutor')
test_eq(source_of(dict(src='web', url='javascript:alert(1)', text='Q.')).url, '')

title: edit
text:
A talk and a walk path have one editor style. Each change saves at once. Then an Undo bar shows, and a history keeps the change, so you can go back. This module is the part of the editor that has no web page:
The web parts (the Undo bar, the history list, the list of rows and its keys) are in abhyasa/core/edit.py.
Import the shelf, the JSON call of the model, the prompts and the fence for source text.

title: edit
text:
The limits
A history keeps at most HISTORY_MOST changes, and at most HISTORY_BYTES of JSON. Older changes drop off first. The newest change always stays.
When you type in a field, the editor saves each time you stop for 600 ms. These saves must not fill the history. A save names its field: the row and the field, such as s5/notes. A save of the same field by the same writer, less than EDIT_JOIN seconds after the first save of the newest change, joins that change. Its Undo goes back to the text before the first save. A join does not reset the clock: one long typing session gives one change for each minute, so an Undo never takes back more than about one minute of typing. A change with no field never joins.
When the newest change alone is over HISTORY_BYTES, the history keeps a short form of it: its id, time, words and writer, with before set to None. Undo cannot give back a change in its short form.

title: edit
text:
The history of one thing
The history of one talk or one walk is one vault document, with the source learning://edits/{kind}/{doc} and the kind edits. For example, the kind is talk and the doc is the id of the talk. Each change has an id, the time at, the words what, the writer who, and before: the whole list of slides or steps before the change. Search never shows these documents.


source

edit_lock
def edit_lock(
    kind:str, doc:str
)-><function RLock at 0x7fabcf3a3ce0>:
The lock of the history of doc. add_edit and pop_edit hold it while they change the thing and its history, so a save and an Undo from two tabs are one step each. Take it before the lock of a walk (journey._jlock), never after it. It is not the Learning._lock of the concepts: a walk save can hold its own lock and then put a concept, so the two locks in the other order could wait on each other.


add_edit keeps one change, newest first. who is you or tutor. before must be JSON. Bad values raise ValueError. With apply, it calls apply() (the save of the change) under edit_lock first, and keeps the change only when the save works. So a save and its change in the history are one step.


source

Learning.add_edit
def add_edit(
    kind:str, doc:str, what:str, who:str, before:list, field:str=None, apply:NoneType=None
)->list:
Keep the change what by who to the document doc of kind, with the state before it. Return the history, newest first. field (such as s5/notes) lets the saves of one field join: the same field and writer, less than EDIT_JOIN seconds after the first save of the newest change. A join keeps the first before and the first time, so the clock does not reset. With apply, call it first under edit_lock; when it raises, nothing is kept.


edits reads the history. edit finds one change by its id, for “Restore this version”.


source

Learning.edit
def edit(
    kind:str, doc:str, eid:str
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
The change eid in the history of doc, or None.




source

Learning.edits
def edits(
    kind:str, doc:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
The history of doc: AttrDict(id, at, what, who, before), newest first.


pop_edit is the Undo: it returns the newest change, so the editor can write back its before. With eid, it acts only when that change is still the newest, so an old Undo bar does nothing. With apply, the Undo is one step under edit_lock: it looks at the newest change, calls apply(change) to write back its before, and takes the change out of the history only when apply works. When apply raises, the change stays. A change in its short form (before is None) comes out with no apply: the editor says that it cannot undo it. drop_edits removes the history of a thing that you removed.


source

Learning.drop_edits
def drop_edits(
    kind:str, doc:str
):
Remove the history of doc.




source

Learning.pop_edit
def pop_edit(
    kind:str, doc:str, eid:str=None, apply:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
Undo the newest change of doc: apply(change) writes back its before, then the change leaves the history. None when there is none, or eid is not the newest.


A test vault. It keeps 50 of 55 changes. The newest is first.

from abhyasa.store import temp_learning


lr = temp_learning()
for k in range(55): lr.add_edit('talk', 't1', f'change {k}', 'you', [dict(id=f's{k}')])
test_eq(len(lr.edits('talk', 't1')), 50); test_eq(lr.edits('talk', 't1')[0].what, 'change 54')

Undo takes out the newest change and returns it with its state before.

test_eq(lr.pop_edit('talk', 't1').what, 'change 54'); test_eq(len(lr.edits('talk', 't1')), 49)
test_eq(lr.edits('talk', 't1')[0].before, [dict(id='s53')])

An Undo with an id that is not the newest does nothing.

old = lr.edits('talk', 't1')[1].id
test_is(lr.pop_edit('talk', 't1', old), None); test_eq(len(lr.edits('talk', 't1')), 49)
test_eq(lr.edit('talk', 't1', old).what, 'change 52')

Two saves of the same field, by the same writer, are one change. Its before is the text before the first save.

lr.add_edit('walk', 'w1', 'Changed the note of step 2.', 'you', ['a'], field='s2/note')
lr.add_edit('walk', 'w1', 'Changed the note of step 2.', 'you', ['b'], field='s2/note')
test_eq(len(lr.edits('walk', 'w1')), 1); test_eq(lr.edits('walk', 'w1')[0].before, ['a'])

Another writer, another field, or no field gives a new change, also with the same words.

lr.add_edit('walk', 'w1', 'Changed the note of step 2.', 'tutor', ['c'], field='s2/note')
lr.add_edit('walk', 'w1', 'Changed the note of step 2.', 'tutor', ['d'], field='s3/note')
lr.add_edit('walk', 'w1', 'Changed the note of step 2.', 'tutor', ['e']); lr.add_edit('walk', 'w1', 'Changed the note of step 2.', 'tutor', ['f'])
test_eq(len(lr.edits('walk', 'w1')), 5)

A join does not reset the clock: a save more than EDIT_JOIN seconds after the first save of the change is a new change.

lr.add_edit('walk', 'w2', 'Changed the title of step 1.', 'you', ['a'], field='s1/title')
rows = lr._edit_rows('walk', 'w2'); rows[0]['at'] -= EDIT_JOIN - 1; lr._put_edits('walk', 'w2', rows)   # the first save, 59 s ago
lr.add_edit('walk', 'w2', 'Changed the title of step 1.', 'you', ['b'], field='s1/title')
test_eq(len(lr.edits('walk', 'w2')), 1)
rows = lr._edit_rows('walk', 'w2'); rows[0]['at'] -= 2; lr._put_edits('walk', 'w2', rows)   # now 61 s ago
lr.add_edit('walk', 'w2', 'Changed the title of step 1.', 'you', ['c'], field='s1/title')
test_eq([e.before for e in lr.edits('walk', 'w2')], [['c'], ['a']])

The history is in the vault, so a new Learning on the same vault reads it. Bad values raise ValueError.

from abhyasa.store import Learning


test_eq(len(Learning(lr.vault).edits('talk', 't1')), 49)
for bad in [dict(kind='a/b'), dict(doc='t1\n'), dict(kind='talk\n'), dict(doc='ṭ1'), dict(who='me'), dict(what='  '), dict(before=[object()])]:
    a = dict(kind='talk', doc='t1', what='x', who='you', before=[]) | bad
    test_fail(lambda: lr.add_edit(**a), exc=ValueError)

Undo with apply is one step. When apply fails, the change stays, so a later Undo can try again. When it works, the change goes.

state = dict(slides=['new'])
lr.add_edit('talk', 't2', 'Changed slide 1.', 'you', ['old'], apply=lambda: state.update(slides=['new']))
def broken(e): raise OSError('disk full')
test_fail(lambda: lr.pop_edit('talk', 't2', apply=broken), exc=OSError)
test_eq(len(lr.edits('talk', 't2')), 1)
test_eq(lr.pop_edit('talk', 't2', apply=lambda e: state.update(slides=e.before)).what, 'Changed slide 1.')
test_eq(state['slides'], ['old']); test_eq(lr.edits('talk', 't2'), [])

A save that fails keeps no change.

test_fail(lambda: lr.add_edit('talk', 't2', 'Changed slide 1.', 'you', ['x'], apply=lambda: 1/0), exc=ZeroDivisionError)
test_eq(lr.edits('talk', 't2'), [])

A newest change that is too large alone keeps its short form, so the cap always holds. Undo then cannot give it back.

big = ['x' * (HISTORY_BYTES + 10)]
lr.add_edit('talk', 't3', 'Changed slide 1.', 'you', ['a']); lr.add_edit('talk', 't3', 'Changed all slides.', 'you', big)
es = lr.edits('talk', 't3')
test_eq(len(es), 1); test_eq((es[0].what, es[0].before), ('Changed all slides.', None))
assert len(json.dumps(lr._edit_rows('talk', 't3'))) <= HISTORY_BYTES
test_eq(lr.pop_edit('talk', 't3', apply=lambda e: 1/0).before, None)   # no apply for a short form

A history never shows in a search, and drop_edits removes it.

test_eq([h for h in lr.search('Changes to the talk') if h['kind'] == 'edits'], [])
lr.drop_edits('talk', 't1'); test_eq(lr.edits('talk', 't1'), [])

title: edit
section: The Undo of a walk path
text:
The Undo of a walk path
A walk step has fields that the editor changes (EDIT_FIELDS: the status, the why, the note, the check, its code, the passage and the merged ideas), and fields that the walk writes as you learn: the progress (done, qid, read_at), the side walks, the notebook, the Leela stamp and the research state. The tutor note is content: you edit it, so an Undo gives back the old note. The walk can write its own fields after you changed the path. An Undo must not lose them.
restore_steps gives the order of before. Each step that is also in now (by its slug) is the step of now, with the editor fields of before. It also takes the read of now when research wrote it (researched=True) and the step in before had no passage. A step that is only in before comes back as it was. A step that is only in now goes: the change being undone added it.
The code of a step belongs to its check (qid). When the walk made the check again after the change, the old code does not fit the new check, so the step keeps the code of now. undo_line then gives the line CODE_GONE, for the editor to show.


source

undo_line
def undo_line(
    before:list, now:list
)->str:
CODE_GONE when restore_steps(before, now) keeps the code of a check that the walk made again; else ’’.




source

restore_steps
def restore_steps(
    before:list, now:list
)->list:
The steps of before in their order. A slug that is also in now is the step of now with the EDIT_FIELDS of before, but a passage that research wrote after before, and the code of a check made again, stay.


Step a moves back to the first place. It keeps the passage that research found, and b keeps its outcome.

before = [dict(slug='a', read=dict(text='')), dict(slug='b', read=dict(text='p'))]
now = [dict(slug='b', read=dict(text='p'), done=dict(outcome='solid')), dict(slug='a', read=dict(text='w', researched=True))]
out = restore_steps(before, now)
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in out], ['a', 'b']); test_eq(out[0]['read']['text'], 'w'); test_eq(out[1]['done'], dict(outcome='solid'))

A step that the change added goes. A step that the change removed comes back. before does not change.

out = restore_steps([dict(slug='a'), dict(slug='c', qid='q1')], [dict(slug='a', qid='q2'), dict(slug='new')])
test_eq(out, [dict(slug='a', qid='q2'), dict(slug='c', qid='q1')])
test_eq(restore_steps(before, now)[0]['read'], dict(text='w', researched=True)); test_eq(before[0]['read'], dict(text=''))

An Undo of a note edit gives back the old note: the note is content, not a run field.

test_eq(restore_steps([dict(slug='a', note='old')], [dict(slug='a', note='new')]), [dict(slug='a', note='old')])

A side walk, a notebook, a Leela stamp and the research state that the walk wrote after the snapshot stay. The editor fields come back.

b = [dict(slug='a', status='skip', research='pending')]
n = [dict(slug='a', status='todo', detours=[dict(slug='x')], nb=dict(cells=[]), leela_at=7., research='none')]
test_eq(restore_steps(b, n), [dict(slug='a', status='skip', detours=[dict(slug='x')], nb=dict(cells=[]), leela_at=7., research='none')])

A step whose check the walk made again keeps the new code and the new check, and undo_line says so. With the same check, the old code comes back.

b, n = [dict(slug='a', qid='q1', code=dict(stub='old'))], [dict(slug='a', qid='q2', code=dict(stub='new'))]
test_eq(restore_steps(b, n), [dict(slug='a', qid='q2', code=dict(stub='new'))]); test_eq(undo_line(b, n), CODE_GONE)
n = [dict(slug='a', qid='q1', code=dict(stub='edited'))]
test_eq(restore_steps(b, n)[0]['code'], dict(stub='old')); test_eq(undo_line(b, n), '')

title: edit
text:
Rewrite with an instruction
You tell the tutor what to change, such as “simpler” or “add an example”. The tutor rewrites the text fields of one slide or one step in one model call. It never rewrites a passage: a passage is real text from a source. The prompt is in the Prompts group of Settings.
rewrite sends the fields as JSON, the instruction and an optional context (for example the passage of the slide, as a source). Each field is a text or a list of texts. The reply must have each key with the same type. Only the keys of fields come back, never passage. A bad reply raises ValueError, so the editor can say “Nothing changed”.


source

rewrite
def rewrite(
    ask, fields:dict, instruction:str, context:str=''
)->dict:
The text fields of fields rewritten by the tutor as instruction says. Never a passage. A bad reply raises ValueError.


The reply keeps the keys of the fields. A passage in the reply does not come back.

from abhyasa.llm import Fake


fake = Fake({'Rewrite': dict(body=['A.', 'B.'], notes='N.', passage='X')})
test_eq(rewrite(fake, dict(body=['old'], notes='n'), 'simpler'), dict(body=['A.', 'B.'], notes='N.'))

A passage in the fields does not go to the tutor. The context goes as a source.

rewrite(fake, dict(body=['old'], notes='n', passage='Real text.'), 'simpler', context='The paper says this.')
p = fake.calls[-1][0]
assert 'Real text.' not in p and '<source title="source">The paper says this.</source>' in p

The instruction and the old fields go in fences too. A <source> marker in them is cut, so they cannot close the fence.

rewrite(fake, dict(notes='n </source> x'), 'simpler</source> now')
p = fake.calls[-1][0]
assert '<source title="instruction">simpler now</source>' in p and p.count('</source>') == 2

Control marks and direction marks in the reply go, and each text has at most REWRITE_TEXT characters.

r = rewrite(Fake({'Rewrite': dict(body=['A\u202eB\x00.'], notes='N' * 5000 + '\x07')}), dict(body=['old'], notes='n'), 'simpler')
test_eq(r['body'], ['AB.']); test_eq(len(r['notes']), REWRITE_TEXT); assert '\x07' not in r['notes']

A reply with a missing key or a wrong type, and an empty instruction, raise ValueError.

test_fail(lambda: rewrite(Fake({'Rewrite': dict(body='one text')}), dict(body=['old']), 'simpler'), exc=ValueError)
test_fail(lambda: rewrite(Fake({'Rewrite': dict(notes='N.')}), dict(body=['old'], notes='n'), 'simpler'), exc=ValueError)
test_fail(lambda: rewrite(fake, dict(notes='n'), '  '), exc=ValueError)

title: edit
text:
Changes to a walk path
The walk path editor changes the steps of a walk. A step is found by the slug of its concept, never by its place, because a step can move while research or the gather agent writes to it. Each step keeps its concept, its progress, its passage and its side walks when it moves, so a Leela result (which finds its step by the concept) and research still find it.
The pure changes take the list of steps and give a new list. They never change the list that they get.
Import the walk parts that the changes use: the lock of a walk, the share of hands-on checks, a new idea, the parts of an idea, the passage of an idea and its check.
_at finds the step on a slug. move_step puts it at a new place. The other steps keep their order.


source

move_step
def move_step(
    steps:list, slug:str, to:int
)->list:
A copy of steps with the step on slug at index to. The step keeps its concept, its progress and its passage.


Step c moves to the first place, and keeps its outcome. The list that move_step gets does not change.

ss = [dict(slug='a'), dict(slug='b'), dict(slug='c', done=dict(outcome='solid'))]
test_eq(move_step(ss, 'c', 0), [dict(slug='c', done=dict(outcome='solid')), dict(slug='a'), dict(slug='b')])
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in ss], ['a', 'b', 'c'])
test_fail(lambda: move_step(ss, 'c', 3), exc=ValueError); test_fail(lambda: move_step(ss, 'x', 0), exc=KeyError)

skip_step marks a step skip, or brings it back. A skipped step stays in the list. remove_step takes a step out. The attempts of a removed step stay in the vault: the editor never changes them.


source

remove_step
def remove_step(
    steps:list, slug:str
)->list:
A copy of steps without the step on slug.




source

skip_step
def skip_step(
    steps:list, slug:str, on:bool=True
)->list:
A copy of steps with the step on slug skipped, or brought back (on=False).



test_eq(skip_step(ss, 'b')[1]['status'], 'skip'); test_eq(skip_step(skip_step(ss, 'b'), 'b', False)[1]['status'], 'todo')
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in remove_step(ss, 'a')], ['b', 'c'])

merge_steps joins a step with the next step. It keeps the concept, the check and the passage of the first step. The passage of the second step goes in read.also, so both passages stay. The last step has no next step to join.


source

merge_steps
def merge_steps(
    steps:list, slug:str
)->list:
A copy of steps with the step on slug joined with the next step: the first concept and its passage stay, and the second passage goes in read.also.



m = merge_steps([dict(slug='a', read=dict(text='A.')), dict(slug='b', read=dict(text='B.')), dict(slug='c')], 'a')
test_eq(m, [dict(slug='a', read=dict(text='A.', also=[dict(text='B.')]), merged=['b']), dict(slug='c')])
test_fail(lambda: merge_steps(m, 'c'), contains='last idea')

hands_count comes from journey: the hands-on checks that are not notebooks, the steps that are not skipped, and the notebook steps. The editor shows the share. It only warns: nothing stops a walk with more.

test_eq(hands_count([dict(check=dict(kind='demo')), dict(check=dict(kind='notebook'), hands='notebook'), dict(check=dict(kind='short'), status='skip')]), (1, 2, 1))


The save check
check_steps gives the problems of a list of steps: a step with no concept, a concept that is in the walk twice, a check kind that is not known, a control mark in a note or a check question, and a notebook spec that validate_nb_spec refuses. A notebook spec that did not change is not checked again. clean_step takes the control marks out of the note and the check question, so an old step with a mark does not stop the next change.


source

clean_step
def clean_step(
    s:dict
)->dict:
Step s with no control marks in its note and its check question.




source

check_steps
def check_steps(
    steps:list, old:tuple=()
)->list:
The problems of the walk steps steps, each as one line; an empty list when there is none. A notebook spec that is the same in old is not checked again.



test_eq(check_steps([dict(slug='a', check=dict(kind='demo'), note='Fine.')]), [])
test_eq(check_steps([dict(slug='a'), dict(slug='a')]), ['Idea 2 is in the walk twice.'])
test_eq(check_steps([dict(slug='a', check=dict(kind='quiz'))]), ["Idea 1 has a check kind that abhyasa does not know: 'quiz'."])
test_eq(check_steps([dict(slug='a', check=dict(q='Why\u202e?'))]), ['The check question of idea 1 has a control mark.'])
test_eq(clean_step(dict(slug='a', note='N\x07.', check=dict(q='Q\u202e?'))), dict(slug='a', note='N.', check=dict(q='Q?')))

A notebook spec that is not valid is refused. The same spec in old is not checked again.

bad = [dict(slug='a', nb=dict(task='x'))]
assert check_steps(bad)[0].startswith('The notebook of idea 1 is not valid')
test_eq(check_steps(bad, old=bad), [])



Side walks follow their step
A side walk keeps the place of the step that opened it (parent.step). After a change, reparent gives each side walk the new place of the same step, found by its concept. A side walk whose step left the walk keeps its old place.


source

reparent
def reparent(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, jid:str, before:list, after:list
)->list:
Give each side walk of walk jid the place in after of the step that it was opened from. The key is the concept of that step (parent.idea; an old side walk gets it from its place in before), and it never changes. A step that a merge joined maps to the step that it joined. A removed step gives no place (step None) until an Undo brings the step back. Return the side walk ids that changed.



import abhyasa.journey


lr = temp_learning()
lr.put_journey(dict(id='w1', title='W', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='a'), dict(slug='b')]))
lr.put_journey(dict(id='side1', title='S', mode='walk', steps=[], parent=dict(walk='w1', step=1)))
b = lr.journey('w1').steps
test_eq(reparent(lr, 'w1', b, move_step(b, 'b', 0)), ['side1']); test_eq(lr.journey('side1').parent, dict(walk='w1', step=0, idea='b'))
lr.merge_journey('side1', parent=dict(walk='w1', step=1, idea='b'))   # back to step `b`, for the tests below



One change, kept with its Undo
edit_walk makes one change to walk jid and keeps it in the history, as one step. It takes edit_lock first and then the lock of the walk (_jlock), so a save from research or the gather agent waits. It reads the steps, applies op, and checks the result with check_steps. A change that changes nothing keeps nothing. what says what changed; it can be a function of the old and the new steps. A problem raises ValueError, and nothing is saved.


source

edit_walk
def edit_walk(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, jid:str, op, what, who:str='you', field:str=None
)->tuple:
Apply op (old steps -> new steps) to walk jid and keep the change in its history. Return (walk, history); the history is None when nothing changed.


undo_walk takes back the newest change (only when eid is still the newest). It writes back the steps of before with restore_steps, so the progress and a researched passage stay, and the side walks follow. It returns the change and the line of undo_line. restore_walk goes back to the version before one change, and keeps that as a new change, so you can undo it.


source

restore_walk
def restore_walk(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, jid:str, eid:str
)->tuple:
Go back to the version of walk jid before the change eid, as a new change. Return (walk, history).




source

undo_walk
def undo_walk(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, jid:str, eid:str=None
)->tuple:
Undo the newest change of walk jid. Return (change, line); the change is None when there is nothing to undo.


A move keeps its history. Undo gives back the exact old steps, and the side walk goes back to its step.

w, rows = edit_walk(lr, 'w1', lambda ss: move_step(ss, 'b', 0), 'Moved idea 2 up.')
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in w.steps], ['b', 'a']); test_eq(rows[0].what, 'Moved idea 2 up.'); test_eq(lr.journey('side1').parent['step'], 0)
e, line = undo_walk(lr, 'w1')
test_eq(lr.journey('w1').steps, b); test_eq(e.what, 'Moved idea 2 up.'); test_eq(line, ''); test_eq(lr.journey('side1').parent['step'], 1)
test_eq(lr.edits('walk', 'w1'), [])

The key is the concept, so a remove and its Undo put the side walk back on the same step, not on the step that took its place. A merge maps it to the step that it joined.

lr.put_journey(dict(id='w3', title='W', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='a'), dict(slug='b'), dict(slug='c')]))
lr.put_journey(dict(id='side3', title='S', mode='walk', steps=[], parent=dict(walk='w3', step=1)))
s3 = lr.journey('w3').steps
edit_walk(lr, 'w3', lambda ss: remove_step(ss, 'b'), 'Removed “b”.')
test_eq(lr.journey('side3').parent, dict(walk='w3', step=None, idea='b'))
undo_walk(lr, 'w3'); test_eq(lr.journey('side3').parent, dict(walk='w3', step=1, idea='b'))
edit_walk(lr, 'w3', lambda ss: merge_steps(ss, 'a'), 'Merged “a” and “b”.'); test_eq(lr.journey('side3').parent['step'], 0)
undo_walk(lr, 'w3'); test_eq(lr.journey('side3').parent, dict(walk='w3', step=1, idea='b')); test_eq(lr.journey('w3').steps, s3)

A change that changes nothing keeps nothing. A change with a problem raises ValueError and saves nothing.

test_eq(edit_walk(lr, 'w1', lambda ss: ss, 'Nothing.')[1], None)
test_fail(lambda: edit_walk(lr, 'w1', lambda ss: ss + [dict(slug='a')], 'Added a.'), contains='twice')
test_eq(lr.journey('w1').steps, b); test_eq(lr.edits('walk', 'w1'), [])

A restore is a change too, so an Undo takes it back.

edit_walk(lr, 'w1', lambda ss: remove_step(ss, 'a'), 'Removed “a”.')
restore_walk(lr, 'w1', lr.edits('walk', 'w1')[0].id)
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in lr.journey('w1').steps], ['a', 'b']); test_eq(len(lr.edits('walk', 'w1')), 2)



Add and split
add_step adds an idea at place at: by its name (the tutor writes a new concept when the shelf has none), by the slug of a concept from the concept tree, or with a read that you picked from a source. The new step gets a check. With no read, it looks for a passage in the documents of the walk and in sources, as a new walk does. A step with no passage then gets “Find a source” on its page. The model call runs before the locks.
split_step asks the tutor for the smaller parts of an idea (split_parts), then adds each as a step before it, with a passage and a check.


source

split_step
def split_step(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, jid:str, slug:str, sources:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Split the step on slug of walk jid: the tutor finds its parts, and each goes before it as a step with a passage and a check. Keep the change. Return the walk.




source

add_step
def add_step(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, jid:str, at:int, name:str='', slug:str='', read:dict | None=None,
    sources:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Add an idea to walk jid at index at: by name, by the slug of a concept, or with the picked passage read. Keep the change. Return the walk.


An idea from the concept tree goes at its place, with a check. The same idea a second time is refused.

lr.put('Softmax', 'Turns scores into weights that add to 1.', 'ml')
w = add_step(lr, None, 'w1', 1, slug='softmax')
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in w.steps], ['a', 'softmax', 'b']); assert w.steps[1]['check']['kind'] in CHECK_KINDS
test_fail(lambda: add_step(lr, None, 'w1', 0, slug='softmax'), contains='already')

An idea by a new name: the tutor writes the concept. A split adds the parts before the idea.

from abhyasa.llm import Fake


f = Fake({'The idea: ': dict(name='Temperature', statement='A number that divides the scores.'),
          'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[dict(name='Exponent', statement='e to a power.', aliases=[], prereqs=[])])})
test_eq(add_step(lr, f, 'w1', 99, name='Temperature').steps[-1]['slug'], 'temperature')
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in split_step(lr, f, 'w1', 'softmax').steps], ['a', 'exponent', 'softmax', 'b', 'temperature'])
test_eq(lr.edits('walk', 'w1')[0].what, 'Split “Softmax”: added 1 idea.')



Real passages to pick
passages gives the real passages that a step can take: the paragraphs of the documents of the walk (its source, the pages of a link, and the document of each passage), word for word. A walk with no document gives the passages that ground finds in sources for the name of the idea. q keeps the passages that have each word of q. The passages that name the idea come first. pick_read gives the read of a text that you picked, only when it is in one of these passages word for word (verbatim). The tutor never writes a passage.


source

pick_read
def pick_read(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, j, i:int=None, text:str='', name:str='', sources:NoneType=None
)->dict:
The read of step i (or of a new idea name) from the picked text. It must be in a real passage of the walk word for word; else ValueError.




source

passages
def passages(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, j, i:int=None, q:str='', name:str='', sources:NoneType=None
)->list:
The real passages that step i of walk j (or a new idea name) can pick, as AttrDict(text, place, src); with q, only the ones with each word of q.


A walk on a pasted paper: its paragraphs are the passages. A text that is in a paragraph is picked word for word. A made-up text is refused.

d = lr.vault.add([(0, 'Softmax turns a list of scores into weights. Each weight is above 0, and the weights add to 1.'),
                  (1, 'A large score makes softmax almost one-hot, so the other weights get very small gradients.')], 'A paper on softmax', source='/tmp/sm.pdf', kind='pdf')
pw = AttrDict(id='pw', title='P', steps=[dict(slug='softmax', read=None)], source=dict(shelf='store', doc_id=d['doc_id']))
ps = passages(lr, pw, 0)
test_eq(len(ps), 2); test_eq(ps[0].src['page'], 1); assert 'p. 2' in ps[1].place
test_eq([p.src['page'] for p in passages(lr, pw, 0, q='one-hot')], [2])
test_eq(pick_read(lr, pw, 0, 'Each weight is above 0, and the weights add to 1.')['text'], 'Each weight is above 0, and the weights add to 1.')
test_fail(lambda: pick_read(lr, pw, 0, 'Words that the tutor made up for this idea.'), exc=ValueError)
assert all(pick_read(lr, pw, 0, p.text) for p in ps)   # each passage that the picker shows is one that a pick takes



Improve the walk
The learner can tell the tutor what to change in a walk, in their own words: make it simpler or harder, or add an idea, with a link as its source. propose asks the tutor for a short list of changes. Each change uses one op of the walk editor: add (with a name, and a link when the learner gave one), remove, skip, move (with to, the new place from 1), split, easier or harder (the depth of the check goes down or up by one). Each change has a one-line why. A change that names no idea of the walk, an op that the editor does not have, or a link that the learner did not give is left out. links_in finds the links in the words of the learner.


source

propose
def propose(
    ask, j, names:dict, words:str, weak:tuple=(), links:tuple=()
)->list:
The changes to walk j that the tutor proposes for the words of the learner, each as AttrDict(op, slug, name, link, to, why). names maps a slug to its name; weak are the slugs of the ideas that the learner got wrong or was not sure of; links are the links that abhyasa filed.




source

links_in
def links_in(
    words:str
)->list:
The web links in words, in order, each one time, with no mark at the end.


A walk of three ideas. The learner asks for a simpler walk and gives a link: the tutor proposes an easier check, an idea from the link, and a change with a key that the walk does not have, which is left out.

test_eq(links_in('Add attention, from https://example.org/attn. And https://example.org/attn again'), ['https://example.org/attn'])
iw = lr.put_journey(dict(id='iw', title='Softmax', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug=s, status='todo', check=dict(way='words', kind='short', depth=3)) for s in ('a', 'softmax', 'b')]))
CH = dict(changes=[dict(op='easier', idea='softmax', why='The check asks less.'), dict(op='add', name='Attention', link='https://example.org/attn', to=2, why='You asked for it.'),
                   dict(op='remove', idea='nope', why='x'), dict(op='fly', idea='a')])
f = Fake({'You propose changes to one learning walk': CH})
cs = propose(f, iw, {'softmax': 'Softmax'}, 'Simpler please. Add attention, from https://example.org/attn', links=['https://example.org/attn'])
test_eq([(c.op, c.slug, c.name, c.link, c.to) for c in cs], [('easier', 'softmax', '', '', None), ('add', '', 'Attention', 'https://example.org/attn', 2)])
assert '<source title="learner">' in f.calls[0][0] and 'idea softmax: Softmax' in f.calls[0][0]

improve_walk applies the changes that the learner kept, as one change with one Undo. It writes the new ideas before it takes the lock: an idea from a link gets its passage from the documents of that link (docs maps a link to them), word for word. The ideas that the changes do not touch keep their progress.


source

improve_walk
def improve_walk(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, jid:str, changes:list, sources:NoneType=None, docs:dict=None
)->tuple:
Apply changes (from propose) to walk jid as one change of the tutor, with one Undo. docs maps a link to its filed documents. Return (walk, history).


The learner keeps both changes. Softmax gets an easier check, and Attention comes in at place 2, with its passage from the filed link. Undo takes back both.

da = lr.vault.add([(0, 'Attention mixes the values by weights. The weights come from the scores of each query against each key.')], 'Attention notes', source='https://example.org/attn', kind='web')
dl = [dict(shelf='store', doc_id=da['doc_id'])]
f.rules['The idea: '] = dict(name='Attention', statement='Mixing values by weights.')
w, rows = improve_walk(lr, f, 'iw', cs, docs={'https://example.org/attn': dl})
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in w.steps], ['a', 'attention', 'softmax', 'b'])
test_eq((w.steps[2]['check']['depth'], w.steps[2]['check']['why']), (2, EASIER))
assert w.steps[1]['read']['text'].startswith('Attention mixes the values') and w.steps[1]['read']['doc_id'] == dl[0]['doc_id']
test_eq(rows[0].what, 'Improved the walk: 2 changes.')
undo_walk(lr, 'iw')
test_eq([(s['slug'], s['check']['depth']) for s in lr.journey('iw').steps], [('a', 3), ('softmax', 3), ('b', 3)])

title: prompts
text:
Each prompt of the tutor has two parts. The variable parts (the concept, the thread, the JSON shape) stay in code. The instruction text is in this registry. Each prompt has a name, a plain label, a note on what it changes, and its default text from code. The Settings page shows each prompt, and you can change its text there. The tutor reads each prompt when it calls the model. Thus a change works on the next question, with no restart.
Import the tools that this module uses. The settings come from settings only when a prompt is read, so the import stays light.

title: prompts
text:
The registry
register adds a prompt to PROMPTS and returns its default text. A check can refuse a bad text: it raises ValueError with a plain message.


source

register
def register(
    name:str, label:str, note:str, dflt:str, check:NoneType=None
)->str:
Add the prompt name with a plain label, a note on what it changes, its dflt text and an optional check. Return dflt.


lines gives the lines of a text that are not empty. need_lines makes a check that refuses a text without exactly n such lines.


source

need_lines
def need_lines(
    n:int, what:str
):
A check that refuses a text that does not have n lines that are not empty.




source

lines
def lines(
    text:str
)->list:
The lines of text that are not empty, without spaces at the ends.

title: prompts
text:
Read and save
prompt gives the saved text of a prompt, else its default. set_prompt saves a text in the settings, under the prompts key. An empty text, or a text that is the same as the default, removes the saved text. Then the default is in use again, also when a new version changes the default.


source

set_prompt
def set_prompt(
    name:str, text:str=''
)->str:
Save the text of the prompt name. An empty text uses the default. A text that fails the check raises ValueError. Return the text in use.




source

prompt
def prompt(
    name:str
)->str:
The text of the prompt name now: the saved text, else the default.




source

saved
def saved()->dict:
The saved prompt texts: name -> text.

title: prompts
text:
Tests
A small prompt with a check of 2 lines. Its default is in use at first.

register('greet', 'Greeting', 'The first line.', 'Say hello.\nSay your name.', need_lines(2, 'The greeting'))
test_eq(prompt('greet'), 'Say hello.\nSay your name.')

A saved text is in use at once, and the settings keep it under prompts.

test_eq(set_prompt('greet', 'Say hi.\r\nSay your job.\n'), 'Say hi.\nSay your job.')
test_eq((prompt('greet'), saved()), ('Say hi.\nSay your job.', {'greet': 'Say hi.\nSay your job.'}))

A text that fails the check is refused with a plain message, and the saved text stays.

test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('greet', 'Only one line.'), contains='needs 2 lines')
test_eq(prompt('greet'), 'Say hi.\nSay your job.')

An empty text, or only spaces, removes the saved text, so the default is in use again. A text that is the same as the default is not kept.

test_eq(set_prompt('greet', '  \n '), 'Say hello.\nSay your name.')
set_prompt('greet', 'Say hello.\nSay your name.')
test_eq(saved(), {})

An unknown name is an error. Then the test prompt goes away.

test_fail(lambda: prompt('nope'))
del PROMPTS['greet']

title: demo
text:
A demo is one interactive figure from rupaka. It asks the learner for a prediction first. It shows the result after the learner locks in the prediction. This module keeps demos on the learning shelf. Concepts and attempts are on the same shelf. The module decides when the tutor makes a demo. It runs that job in the background, so the learner never waits.
Import the modules that this notebook uses.

title: demo
text:
Storage
A demo is one vault document. Its source is learning://demo/<slug>, its kind is demo, and its meta holds the spec.







meta
value




concept
the slug of the concept, the link


spec
the rupaka spec


schema, rupaka
the schema of the spec, and the rupaka version that checked it


by
model:<name> or hand


checked
the time of the last passing check, or None


aim
'' for a demo, 'order' for an order check (the learner puts steps in order), 'simpler' for a simpler demo after a miss, or '3d' for a 3D explainer


stats
shown: predictions made; right: predictions that were right



The text of the document is the title, the question, the gate prompts, the captions and the labels of the images, so hybrid search finds a demo.


source

demo_text
def demo_text(
    spec
)->str:
The searchable text of a demo: title, ask, gate prompts, captions and the labels of pixels images.


put_demo adds a demo, or replaces the demo with the same slug. It keeps the stats of the old demo. The vault keeps only one document for each text. So the text ends with the slug and the concept, and two demos with the same spec stay two documents. A model picks the id of a spec. When another concept, another aim or another ask already uses that id, put_demo puts the slug of the concept (and the aim, and the key of the ask) in front of the id. A lock keeps the check and the add together, so two demo jobs that run at once do not file under one slug.


source

Learning.put_demo
def put_demo(
    spec:dict, concept:str, by:str='hand', checked:float=None, aim:str='', asked:dict=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Store spec as a demo of concept with the aim aim. asked is the ask that the demo answers: {key, said}.


demo gets one demo by slug. demos lists the demos of a concept, newest first. demo_for gives the newest one. With an aim, demo_for gives the newest demo with that aim. So aim='' gives only a plain demo, never an order check or a simpler demo. A demo that the learner asked for (see Show me below) has the key of the ask. demo_for finds it only with that key, so the plain demo of a concept stays the same.


source

Learning.demo_for
def demo_for(
    concept:str, aim:str=None, key:str=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
The newest demo of concept, or of concept with the aim aim; None when there is none. A demo made for an ask is found only by the key of its ask.




source

Learning.demos
def demos(
    concept:str=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
The demos of concept (or all demos), newest first.




source

Learning.demo
def demo(
    slug:str
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
One demo by slug.



Tests for storage
Make a shelf in a temporary vault, with one concept and the sandhi demo from the rupaka gallery.

from abhyasa.store import temp_learning


lr = temp_learning()
lr.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels at a word boundary join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug='sa-sandhi-vowels')
spec = gallery()['vowel-sandhi']
d = lr.put_demo(spec, 'sa-sandhi-vowels')
test_eq((d.slug, d.concept, d.by, d.stats), ('vowel-sandhi', 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'hand', dict(shown=0, right=0)))

demo_for finds the demo by its concept. demos gives an empty list for an unknown concept. A search for the words of the caption finds the demo.

test_eq(lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels').spec, spec)
test_eq(lr.demos('nope'), [])
test_eq(lr.search('rule stops another starts', kind='demo')[0]['doc_id'], d.doc_id)

The same id for another concept gets a new slug, so it does not replace the first demo.

lr.put('Guna', 'a + i gives e.', 'sanskrit', slug='guna')
test_eq(lr.put_demo(spec, 'guna').slug, 'guna-vowel-sandhi')
test_eq(lr.demo('vowel-sandhi').concept, 'sa-sandhi-vowels')
lr.drop('guna')

An order demo with the same id and the same concept also gets a new slug. demo_for with an aim finds only the demo with that aim. With no aim, it finds the newest demo.

o = lr.put_demo(spec, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', aim='order')
test_eq((o.slug, o.aim), ('sa-sandhi-vowels-order-vowel-sandhi', 'order'))
test_eq((lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels', aim='').slug, lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels', aim='order').slug), ('vowel-sandhi', o.slug))
test_eq(lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels').slug, o.slug)
lr.v.forget(o.doc_id)

A demo is not a concept, so the list of concepts stays the same.

test_eq(lr.concepts().attrgot('slug'), ['sa-sandhi-vowels'])

title: demo
text:
Predictions
The demo page sends each prediction. record_prediction stores it as an attempt with kind='demo'. The attempt has the gate, the pick, the right answer and the “why” line. It counts the prediction in the stats of the demo. A prediction also shows what the learner understands. So it goes to the learner model as an answer. The depth is 2 (recall), or 3 (explain) when the learner wrote why. The rules are the same as for a question. A right pick with high confidence is solid. A wrong pick with high confidence is a misconception.

The misses since a demo
A prediction changes the count of the demo ladder (see below), so the count comes first. since_demo reads the count from your attempts, and rung gives it as a number. You saw a demo when a miss got a demo in its result (the attempt has shown_demo), or when you made a prediction in a demo. A wrong prediction counts as the first miss, because you saw the demo before it. more adds misses that are not saved yet.
keep_rung puts the count on the concept as after_demo (None when no demo is in play). The model reads it: _back waits until the third miss since the demo, so the ladder runs before the step back.


source

keep_rung
def keep_rung(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str
):
Keep the misses since the demo on concept slug as after_demo, for _back in the model.




source

rung
def rung(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, more:int=0
)->int:
The misses on concept slug since you last saw a demo of it, plus more; 0 when no demo is in play.




source

since_demo
def since_demo(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str
):
The misses on concept slug since you last saw a demo of it; None when no demo is in play. A pass ends the count.




source

Learning.record_prediction
def record_prediction(
    slug:str, gate:str, picked, ans, ok:bool, why:str='', context:str='', session:str='', confidence:int=None,
    kind:str='demo', method:str='demo', **meta
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
File one prediction in demo slug as an attempt, count it for method, and update the learner model of its concept. meta goes on the attempt.




source

no_slots
def no_slots(
    t:str
)->str:
t with no sentence that holds an unfilled slot such as {x1}. Text with no slot stays as it is. ’’ when each sentence has a slot.


Record a wrong prediction with a “why” line. Check the attempt fields, the question text and the stats of the demo.

c0 = lr.concept('sa-sandhi-vowels')
a = lr.record_prediction('vowel-sandhi', 'join', 'ai', 'e', False, why='a and i make a diphthong', context='For a + i:', session='s1')
test_eq((a.kind, a.correct, a.thinking, a.demo, a.expected), ('demo', False, 'a and i make a diphthong', 'vowel-sandhi', 'e'))
test_eq(a.question, 'For a + i: What do the two vowels become?')
test_eq(lr.demo('vowel-sandhi').stats, dict(shown=1, right=0))

The question of a prediction never keeps a slot that the browser fills, such as {x1}. With the values in the context, the sentences with a slot go. With no context, the slots get the values of the opening state. Maths stays as it is.

q = 'For x = (2, 3, 1), b = 0.5: Inputs are {x1}, {x2}. Bias is {b}. What is z?'
test_eq(no_slots(q), 'For x = (2, 3, 1), b = 0.5: What is z?')
test_eq(no_slots('Is $\\frac{a}{b}$ above $x_{i}$?'), 'Is $\\frac{a}{b}$ above $x_{i}$?')
sp = dict(state=dict(x1=2), blocks=[dict(type='gate', id='g', prompt='Inputs are {x1}. What is z?')])
test_eq((_asked(sp, 'g', 'For x1 = 2:'), _asked(sp, 'g')), ('For x1 = 2: What is z?', 'Inputs are 2. What is z?'))

A prediction credits the way demo, and keeps the meta of the walk. A step in an order check uses kind='order'.

lrp = temp_learning(); lrp.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Sum 1/(k + rank).', 'ml')
dp = lrp.put_demo(gallery()['reciprocal-rank-fusion'], 'reciprocal-rank-fusion')
gp = first(b['id'] for b in dp.spec['blocks'] if b.get('type') == 'gate')
ap = lrp.record_prediction(dp.slug, gp, 1, 1, True, session='s1', walk='w1', step=2)
assert (ap.kind, ap.method, ap.walk, ap.step) == ('demo', 'demo', 'w1', 2)
assert 'demo' in lrp.stats().methods['ml'] and 'diagram' not in lrp.stats().methods['ml']
assert lrp.record_prediction(dp.slug, gp, 0, 1, False, kind='order', method='order').kind == 'order'
test_fail(lambda: lrp.record_prediction(dp.slug, gp, 1, 1, True, depth=5), contains='meta')   # a key of the attempt cannot be meta

The learner model of the concept gets the prediction. A wrong pick with a “why” line is an answer at depth 3. So the ceiling falls to 3, and the concept is seen one more time.

c1 = lr.concept('sa-sandhi-vowels')
test_eq((c1.ceiling, c1.seen), (3, c0.seen + 1))
test_eq(a.depth, 3)

title: demo
text:
When to make a demo
want_demo says if a concept should get a demo. It is true after checks.demo_misses misses (2 by default) with a saved misconception, or when the concept meta has visual: true.


source

want_demo
def want_demo(
    c
)->bool:
True when concept c should get a demo.


Check the rule. One miss, or misses with no misconception, give no demo. Two misses with a misconception, or visual, give a demo.

assert not want_demo(dict(misses=1, misconceptions=['x'])) and not want_demo(dict(misses=3, misconceptions=[]))
assert want_demo(dict(misses=2, misconceptions=['x'])) and want_demo(dict(visual=True))

title: demo
text:
Feedback on demos and lessons
Under each demo and each lesson, the app shows one quiet row: “Too simple · Just right · Not clear”. “Not clear” opens a short box for a note. The tutor keeps your choice as engine data, and uses it the next time:

on the attempt: feedback_on, verdict and note, and the list fb with each verdict on that attempt, so the history shows it;
on the demo: the counts of each verdict in stats, the last note, and the last feedback;
in the prompt of the next demo or lesson of the idea (demo.feedback and lesson.feedback);
on the ladder: “Too simple” skips the simpler demo, and “Not clear” brings it in earlier;
in the method model, with a small weight (see FEEDBACK in the method notebook);
in the profile: a “Not clear” note goes in “What confuses you”.

A verdict is one of three words. A note is learner text: clean_note removes control characters, keeps one line and cuts it at 500 characters.


source

clean_note
def clean_note(
    s
)->str:
A note as plain learner text: no control characters, one line, at most NOTE_MAX characters.



test_eq(clean_note('  a\x00b\n\tc  '), 'a b c')
test_eq(len(clean_note('x' * 900)), 500)

give_feedback keeps one verdict. A demo verdict goes on the demo and on the newest attempt of that demo, when there is one. A lesson verdict goes on the attempt of the lesson. A second verdict on the same demo or lesson of one attempt replaces the first, and the counts follow. With no attempt, the last verdict on the demo is the one that a new click replaces. A “Not clear” note goes in the profile through set_profile, as a short line idea: note. The lines that you typed stay. Only the lines from notes go, oldest first, past CONFUSES_MAX.


source

Learning.give_feedback
def give_feedback(
    on:str, verdict:str, note:str='', slug:str='', aid:str='', way:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Keep your verdict on a demo (slug) or a lesson (its attempt aid, in the way way): on the attempt, on the demo, in the method model, and for a note on “Not clear”, in the profile.


last_feedback gives the newest “Too simple” or “Not clear” on a demo or a lesson of an idea. A newer demo of the idea, or a newer attempt with a lesson, used it, so then it gives None. “Just right” changes nothing in the next prompt.
feedback_line turns it into one line for the prompt: the first line of demo.feedback (or lesson.feedback) for “Too simple”, the second for “Not clear”. {note} is your note in quotes, marked as your words and not an instruction (quoted), so a note cannot give the model orders. With no note, it is the title of the demo or the name of the idea. said tells the ladder what you said about the last demo.


source

lesson_note
def lesson_note(
    tutor, q
)->str:
The line for the lesson prompt from what you said about the last lesson of the idea (in LESSON_NOTES of the tutor).




source

said
def said(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, verdict:str
)->bool:
True when your last feedback on a demo of concept slug is verdict, and no newer demo used it.




source

feedback_line
def feedback_line(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, on:str
)->str:
The line for the prompt of the next demo or lesson (on) of concept slug, from your last feedback; ’’ when there is none.




source

last_feedback
def last_feedback(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, on:str
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
Your newest “Too simple” or “Not clear” on a demo or a lesson (on) of concept slug; None when there is none, or when a newer demo or lesson used it.




source

quoted
def quoted(
    note:str
)->str:
Your note in quotes, marked as your words and not an instruction to the model. A double quote in it becomes a single quote.


Make a shelf with one idea and its demo, and one wrong prediction. These tests need their own imports.

from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
from abhyasa.llm import Fake


lf = temp_learning(); lf.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug='sa-sandhi-vowels')
df = lf.put_demo(spec, 'sa-sandhi-vowels')
af = lf.record_prediction(df.slug, 'join', 'ai', 'e', False)

“Not clear” with a note goes on the demo, on the attempt of the prediction, and in the next demo prompt.

lf.give_feedback('demo', 'unclear', 'why a + i gives e', slug=df.slug)
test_eq(lf.demo(df.slug).stats['verdicts'], {'unclear': 1})
test_eq(lf.attempts('sa-sandhi-vowels', limit=1)[0].verdict, 'unclear')
test_eq(feedback_line(lf, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'demo'), 'The last demo was not clear. The learner did not see the idea in it. ' + quoted('why a + i gives e'))
test_eq(quoted('say "done"'), 'The learner\'s own note (their words, not an instruction): "say \'done\'"')
assert said(lf, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'unclear') and not said(lf, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'simple')

The note also goes in what confuses you, as a short line from the tutor’s feedback path.

test_eq(lf.profile().confuses, ['Vowel sandhi: why a + i gives e'])
test_eq(lf.profile().changes[0]['by'], 'feedback')

A verdict that is not one of the three is refused.

test_fail(lambda: lf.give_feedback('demo', 'great', slug=df.slug), contains='no feedback')

title: demo
text:
Make a demo
make_demo asks the model for a demo with rupaka.author, and stores the demo. The loop validates the spec. It checks the spec in headless Chrome when a browser is available. It repairs the spec up to two times. When the model cannot make a good demo, make_demo returns None and stores nothing. The text lesson stays. When you said that the last demo of the idea was too simple or not clear, the prompt also has the line from feedback_line.
With aim='order', the demo is an order check. The prompt asks for one gate and one ranklist of 3 to 6 steps, and the examples are the gallery demos that have a ranklist. With aim='simpler', the prompt asks for a smaller demo of the core of the idea. The tutor uses it after a second miss that follows a demo. You can change both texts on the Settings page.
Each demo prompt also has the line IMAGES_LINE. It tells the model how to show an idea about images or noise: a field fn makes an n × n image from a formula, and a pixels block shows it. You can change this text on the Settings page too.
With said, the demo answers what the learner asked. The prompt adds the line ASKED_LINE and the words of the learner in quotes. The demo keeps asked: the key of the ask and its words.


source

make_demo
def make_demo(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, slug:str, first_error:str='', check:NoneType=None, log:list=None,
    aim:str='', said:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
A new checked demo for concept slug with the aim aim, stored on the shelf; None when the model fails. said is the ask of the learner: the demo shows it.


A fake model acts as the agent. It replies with a demo for the concept, or with text that is not JSON.

from abhyasa.llm import Fake


good = {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-by-model'}
fk = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': good})
d = make_demo(lr, fk, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False)
test_eq((d.slug, d.by, d.checked), ('sandhi-by-model', 'model:unknown', None))
test_eq(lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels').slug, 'sandhi-by-model')

When the model never gives a good spec, make_demo stores nothing. The log names the errors.

log = []
test_eq(make_demo(lr, Fake({'You design one interactive demo': 'no demo today'}), 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, log=log), None)
test_eq(len(log), 3)
test_eq(len(lr.demos('sa-sandhi-vowels')), 2)

Each prompt asks for an image on an idea about images or noise. Here the model gives the diffusion demo of the rupaka gallery. Its pixels block shows the field that the formula makes, and the label of the image goes into the text of the demo.

fi = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**gallery()['diffusion-noise'], 'id': 'sandhi-noise'}})
d = make_demo(lr, fi, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False)
assert IMAGES_LINE in fi.calls[0][0] and '`pixels` block' in IMAGES_LINE
test_eq([b['type'] for b in d.spec['blocks']][:2], ['gate', 'pixels'])
assert 'Grid at t = {t}' in demo_text(d.spec)
lr.v.forget(d.doc_id)

A field formula that rupaka cannot read gives the plain expr: error of rupaka. The tutor sends it back to the model, and stores nothing when the model does not repair it.

bad = {**gallery()['diffusion-noise'], 'id': 'sandhi-bad-noise', 'derive': [dict(fn='field', expr='sqrt(1 - t/1000) * (i +', n=16, seed=7, out='img')]}
log = []
test_eq(make_demo(lr, Fake({'You design one interactive demo': bad}), 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, log=log), None)
assert all(any(e.startswith('expr:') or 'expr:' in e for e in l['errors']) for l in log), log

An order demo: the prompt asks for a ranklist and shows the ranklist example from the gallery. The demo keeps its aim.

fo = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-order'}})
d = make_demo(lr, fo, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, aim='order')
p = fo.calls[0][0]
assert ORDER_AIM in p and 'Reciprocal rank fusion' in p and 'Vowel sandhi' not in p.split('Examples')[1]
test_eq((d.slug, d.aim), ('sandhi-order', 'order'))
lr.v.forget(d.doc_id)

A simpler demo: the prompt adds the text of demo.simpler, and the demo keeps the aim simpler. demo_for with aim='' does not give it, also when it is the newest demo.

fs = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-small'}})
d = make_demo(lr, fs, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, aim='simpler')
assert SIMPLER_AIM in fs.calls[0][0] and ORDER_AIM not in fs.calls[0][0]
test_eq((d.slug, d.aim, lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels').slug), ('sandhi-small', 'simpler', 'sandhi-small'))
assert lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels', aim='').aim == ''
lr.v.forget(d.doc_id)

After “Not clear”, the prompt of the next demo has your note. Once that demo is on the shelf, the note is used, so the line is gone.

ff = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-clearer'}})
make_demo(lf, ff, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, aim='simpler')
assert quoted('why a + i gives e') in ff.calls[0][0] and SIMPLER_AIM in ff.calls[0][0]
test_eq(feedback_line(lf, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'demo'), '')

title: demo
text:
The background job
queue_demo runs make_demo in the thread pool of the tutor. It runs only one job at a time for each concept and aim. A second call while the job runs gives the same job. The key of a job is the concept slug, or slug:aim for an aim. A job for an ask adds # and ask_key of the ask, so two asks on one concept are two jobs. job_state tells you if the job runs, failed or is done. job_age gives the seconds since the job started, so a page can stop the wait.


source

job_stage
def job_stage(
    tutor, slug:str, aim:str='', said:str=''
)->str:
The real stage of the demo job of slug: ‘queued’ (another job runs first), ‘writing’ (the model writes the spec), ‘fixing’ (a try failed the checks, and the model writes it again), or ‘none’.




source

job_age
def job_age(
    tutor, slug:str, aim:str='', said:str=''
)->float:
The seconds since the demo job of slug with the aim aim and the ask said started; 0 when there is no job.




source

job_state
def job_state(
    tutor, slug:str, aim:str='', said:str=''
)->str:
‘running’, ‘failed’, ‘done’ or ‘none’ for the demo job of slug with the aim aim and the ask said.




source

queue_demo
def queue_demo(
    tutor, slug:str, first_error:str='', aim:str='', said:str=''
):
Start a background job that makes a demo for slug with the aim aim (and the ask said), or a 3D explainer for the aim 3d; the running job if there is one.




source

ask_key
def ask_key(
    said:str
)->str:
A short key for the ask said: the same words in another case or spacing give the same key.


The stage of a job is real: a job waits while another runs, then the model writes, and a try that fails the checks shows as fixing.

from concurrent.futures import Future


jt = AttrDict(jobs={})
f = Future(); f.log = []; jt.jobs[_key('x', '')] = f
test_eq(job_stage(jt, 'x'), 'queued')
f.set_running_or_notify_cancel(); test_eq(job_stage(jt, 'x'), 'writing')
f.log.append(dict(tries=1, errors=['bad'])); test_eq(job_stage(jt, 'x'), 'fixing')
f.set_result(None); test_eq((job_stage(jt, 'x'), job_stage(jt, 'y')), ('none', 'none'))

title: demo
text:
The demo ladder
Sometimes you see a demo and still miss the idea. Then the tutor goes one rung down a short ladder. It counts only your misses on the idea since you last saw a demo of it. A pass ends the count.



misses since the demo
what the tutor adds




1
a lesson in another way, from the method model: never demo, and never the way that just failed. The demo stays next to it.


2
a simpler demo (the aim simpler), or a job that makes one


3 or more
nothing new. _back in the model sends the next question to the weakest prereq that is not learned.



The setting checks.demo_ladder turns the ladder off. Then a miss gets the plain demo, as before.
since_demo, rung and keep_rung (in the section on predictions) count the misses since the demo.
backed is true when _back sends the next question on the concept to a prereq. After a demo, that is after the third miss since the demo. From then on, the ladder starts no job. So the ladder and the step back do not pull two ways.


source

backed
def backed(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, goal:int=None
)->bool:
True when _back sends the next question on concept slug to a prereq.


other_way picks the way of the lesson on the first rung. It asks the method model for your best text way, as for a weak concept. It leaves out the way that failed. demo is never a text way. failed can also be a list of ways. lesson_way is in LESSON_HOOKS of the tutor. So the tutor writes its usual lesson after the miss, in the other way. A pass on the check of that lesson credits that way. When you said that the demo was too simple, the second miss gets a lesson in another way too, in place of the simpler demo.


source

lesson_way
def lesson_way(
    tutor, q
)->str:
The way of the lesson on the first miss after a demo, and on the second when you said that the demo was too simple; ’’ on another miss, or when the ladder is off.




source

other_way
def other_way(
    learning:abhyasa.store.Learning, slug:str, failed:str=''
)->str:
The best text way for you on concept slug by the method model; never demo, and never the way or the ways failed.


simpler_demo is the second rung. When you said “Not clear” after the newest simpler demo was made, it makes a new one, so your note goes in its prompt. It gives the newest simpler demo, or it queues a job for one. Once _back steps back, it queues nothing.


source

simpler_demo
def simpler_demo(
    tutor, slug:str, first_error:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
The second rung for concept slug: demo, the newest simpler demo; else demo_pending and a queued job; else nothing, once _back steps back. After “Not clear”, an older simpler demo does not count.


A walk has no tutor question after a wrong prediction. demo_lesson uses the same lesson path for a prediction: the gate is the question, and the right pick is the answer. The check of the lesson comes next on the concept, in the way of the lesson.


source

demo_lesson
def demo_lesson(
    tutor, a, way:str
)->str:
A short lesson in the way way after the wrong prediction a, from the lesson path of the tutor.

title: demo
text:
The tutor hook
on_close runs after each question closes (it is in CLOSE_HOOKS). A pass adds nothing. After a miss, it goes down the demo ladder when you saw a demo of the concept:

the first miss keeps the plain demo next to the lesson, which lesson_way wrote in another way;
the second miss gets a simpler demo, or demo_pending with demo_aim='simpler';
a later miss gets nothing new, and ladder in the result says which rung it is.

Your feedback on the demo changes two rungs. After “Too simple”, the second miss gets no simpler demo. After “Not clear”, the first miss already gets the simpler demo.
Else, it attaches the newest plain demo of the concept to the result, and marks the attempt with shown_demo. An order check or a simpler demo is not a plain demo, so on_close does not use it here. When there is no demo yet and the concept wants one, it queues the job. Then it marks the result with demo_pending.


source

on_close
def on_close(
    tutor, q, r
):
After each close: keep the misses since the demo on the concept, and after a miss, go down the demo ladder.



Tests for the hook
Make a session where each answer is a miss with high confidence and the same misconception. The fake model writes the questions, grades, lessons and demos.

from abhyasa.tutor import Tutor
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor


def grader(p, sp): return dict(correct=False, grade=1, first_error='You add the vowels.', misconception='vowels just add', feedback='Look at the rule.')
fk = Fake({'You grade one answer': grader, 'Teach the smallest step': 'One step. Check: what is a + u?',
           'You design one interactive demo': good}, dflt=dict(question='What is a + i?', answer='e', rubric=['e']))
lr2 = temp_learning()
lr2.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug='sa-sandhi-vowels')
t = Tutor(lr2, fk, context=False, pool=ThreadPoolExecutor(1))
def miss():
    q = t.next(focus='sa-sandhi-vowels')
    return t.give_up(q.id, confidence=90)
